A canonical identifier assigned by Customer.io when you add a person. When referencing a person by this value, you must prefix the value with `cio_`. You can [look up a person using the App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/customers/) to find their `cio_id`, but you must prefix this value with `cio_` when using it to reference a person.

track_customer_id.description:
The unique value representing a person. The values you use to identify a person may be an `id`, `email` address, or the `cio_id` (when updating people), depending on your workspace settings. When you reference people by `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_`.

You can't reference a person by their `phone` number here. We determine the identifier type from the shape of the value, so a phone number in the path is treated as an `id`. To identify people by phone number, use the [Track v2 API](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/).

You must use this value to update a person's other identifiers—their `id` or `email`, unless you enable your workspace's [Allow updates to email using ID](/accounts/workspaces#update-email-with-id) setting.

collection_point.description: Where the change came from, like your subscription center or an SMS reply. consent_state.description: The state the change left the person in.

delivery_id.description: The message the person responded to, like the email that contained the unsubscribe link.

from.description: The sender's email address or phone number when the change happened.

profile_identifier.description: The identifier your request used to find the person.

received_on.description: The address or phone number the person's reply came from.

response.description: What the person sent back, like the body of an SMS reply.

sender_id.description: The sender identity the consent applies to, if any.

source_event_id.description: The ID of the activity that produced this record, like the inbound SMS that contained STOP.

topic_id.description: The subscription topic the consent applies to, if any.

topic_name.description: The topic's name when the change happened. Renaming the topic later doesn't change this value.

account_id.description: The account the change belongs to. `0` on workspace audit log entries, which belong to the workspace your key is for.

action.description: The kind of change, like `Created`, `Updated`, or `Deleted`.

changed_from.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, before the change.

changed_to.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, after the change.

data.description: The object as it was saved after the change. The shape depends on `object_type`. A `FailedLogin` entry carries `login_method`, `reason` (like `invalid_password` or `invalid_2fa_code`), and `user_agent`.

id.description: The entry's identifier. Use it as a `cursor` to page through results.

ip_addr.description: The IP address the change came from.

meta.description: Request details recorded with the change.

object_id.description: The identifier of the object that changed. For a `FailedLogin` entry, this is the team member whose sign-in failed.

object_type.description: The kind of object that changed, like `Segment`, `User`, or `FailedLogin`.

related_logs.description: On a `Segment` entry, the latest `Condition` entry for each of the segment's conditions, and the latest `EventType` entry for each event those conditions name, from before the segment changed. Each has its own `changed_from` and `changed_to`, so you can see the segment's rules as they were at the time.

service_account_id.description: The service account that made the change, if any.

timestamp.description: When the change happened, as a unix timestamp in seconds.

user_id.description: The team member who made the change, matching a `user_id` in the response's `users` array. `0` when no signed-in team member made the change, like a failed sign-in.

version.description: The object's version number after the change. For objects that keep one, like segments and automations, it generally goes up as the object changes, but some updates don't change it, so use `id` to put an object's entries in order. The value is `0` on entries that don't record a version.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

filter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment, attribute, and device attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

field.description: The name of the attribute you want to filter against.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* meet the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

device_attribute.description: Filter your audience by the devices people have. We match a person if any of their devices meets the condition. To match people who have any device at all, set `field` to `id` and `operator` to `exists`.

field.description: The name of the device attribute you want to filter against. Use `id` to match people who have a device.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* have a device meeting the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute; `eq` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this device attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

device_attribute.title: device attribute

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: Custom recipients

oneOf.description: An array of emails you want to send the broadcast to. These addresses must already exist; your request cannot create a new person.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

emails.description: An array of email addresses you want to send the broadcast to. These addresses must already exist; your request cannot create a new person. You can list up to 10,000 emails in this field. To send to a larger audience, use `recipients` or `data_file_url`, which don't limit the size of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: Emails

oneOf.description: An array of customer ids that you want to send the broadcast to. These IDs must already exist; your request cannot create a new person.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

ids.description: An array of IDs you want to send a broadcast to. To send to a larger audience, define it with `recipients` or `data_file_url` instead. **NOTE**: If your workspace identifies people by `email`, don't use this option. Identify your audience by `emails` instead.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: IDs

oneOf.description: An array of JSON objects containing `id` or `email` keys and a `data` key. Each object represents a person you want to send the broadcast to and data you want to personalize their message with using liquid.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

per_user_data.description: The people you want to send a broadcast to, with custom data to personalize each message. Each person must already exist in your workspace—a broadcast trigger can't create people. Each entry can be up to 2MB. To personalize messages for a larger audience, use `data_file_url` instead.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Merge data associated with the recipient.

id.description: The ID of the recipient.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Merge data associated with the recipient.

email.description: The email address of the recipient. This address must be unique in your workspace. If more than one person has the same `email` attribute, your request will produce an error.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.description: The URL of a data file with one JSON object per line, using either `id` and `data` or `email` and `data`. The people you reference must already exist in your workspace. The file may be gzip-compressed to reduce transfer size (recommended for large files); if compressed, it must use gzip and the hosting server must return a `Content-Encoding` header set to `gzip` when the file is downloaded.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

data_file_url.description: The URL of a JSON Lines file with one person per line, using `id` and `data` or `email` and `data`. The people you reference must already exist in your workspace. The file can be up to 10GB, and each line can be up to 2MB. The file may be gzip-compressed to reduce transfer size (recommended for large files); if compressed, it must use gzip and the hosting server must return a `Content-Encoding` header set to `gzip` when the file is downloaded.

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

cio_subscription_preferences.description: A person's [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/) preferences. Use JSON dot notation, such as `cio_subscription_preferences.topics.topic_<id>`, to update one topic without replacing others.

additionalProperties.description: Boolean preference for a topic named `topic_<id>`; `true` subscribes, `false` unsubscribes, and empty or missing values use the topic default. Find topic IDs with [getTopics](/integrations/api/app/tag/subscription-center/getTopics/).

topics.description: Contains active topics in your workspace, named `topic_<id>`.

collectionDeleteField.description: An attribute that marks a row for deletion, like `deleted`. When a row in a write request or a synced file sets this attribute to `true`, or to the text `true`, `1`, or `yes` in any case, Customer.io deletes the row with the same key instead of saving it. Deleting a key that doesn't exist does nothing. Customer.io never keeps a row that this attribute marks. When you create or replace a collection, Customer.io leaves marked rows out. When you set a delete field on an existing collection, Customer.io deletes the rows it already marks. A row that isn't marked keeps the attribute as you sent it. The delete field can't be the same as the key field. Send an empty string to remove it.

collectionKeyField.description: The attribute that holds each row's unique key, like `sku`, similar to a primary key in a database table. Set a key field to add, change, delete, or read individual rows without replacing the whole collection. Each row needs a unique, non-empty string or number in this attribute, up to 1,024 bytes.

bytes.description: The size of the collection in bytes.

created_at.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

delete_field.description: The attribute that marks a row for deletion in a write request or a synced file. Absent when the collection has no delete field.

id.description: The identifier for the collection. This is how you'll reference the collection from the API.

key_field.description: The attribute that holds each row's unique key. Absent when the collection has no key field.

name.description: The name of the collection. This is how you'll reference the collection in liquid, e.g. `{{collection_name.data_property}}`.

rows.description: Represents the number of objects in the `data` array or CSV rows in your collection schema.

schema.description: Lists the top-level keys that you can reference within this collection. Customer.io does not enforce any of these keys as required from your `data`.

updated_at.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

bucket.description: The bucket, or for Azure, the container.

id.description: The identifier for the source. Send it as `source_id` when you write to a collection.

name.description: A name that helps you recognize the source.

prefix.description: A folder in the bucket, like `imports`. When you set a prefix, Customer.io only reads files within it, and a write request's `path` is relative to it. Leave it out to read the whole bucket.

provider.description: The storage service that holds the bucket.

region.description: The AWS region of an S3 bucket.

collectionSourceName.description: A name that helps you recognize the source.

collectionSourcePrefix.description: A folder in the bucket, like `imports`. When you set a prefix, Customer.io only reads files within it, and a write request's `path` is relative to it. Leave it out to read the whole bucket.

last_error.description: The most recent error. Absent when the sync hasn't had an error.

message.example: could not read daily/2026-11-02.csv: fetch failed: HTTP 403 status

last_file.description: The last file that Customer.io loaded. Absent until the first file loads.

version.description: The storage provider's version ID for the file.

next_run_at.description: When Customer.io next checks the folder. Absent when the next check isn't scheduled yet.

poll_hours.description: How often Customer.io checks the folder for new or changed files, in hours.

prefix.description: The folder that the sync watches, relative to the source's `prefix`.

source_id.description: The source bucket that the sync reads files from.

state.description: `failed` means the last check stopped at a file that Customer.io couldn't load. Customer.io tries that file again at the next check.

code.description: Why Customer.io rejected the row.

file.description: The path of the file that held the row.

file_version.description: The storage provider's version ID for the file.

key.description: The row's key, when it has one.

row.description: The row's position in the file, starting at 1. In a CSV file, the header row doesn't count, so row 1 is the first row of data.

code.description: If the write request's `state` is `failed`, the code explains why. A write of up to 500 rows saves nothing when it fails, and a larger write keeps the rows it saved before it failed. `source-refused` means Customer.io couldn't download the file, or the source is gone or unusable. `replace-unfinished` means an earlier replacement stopped partway, so you need to replace the collection's rows again.

id.description: The identifier for the write request. Use it to look up the write's status.

items.description: For a write request that failed with `items`, up to 500 of the rows that Customer.io rejected. Customer.io didn't save any of the rows.

code.description: Why the row failed.

index.description: The row's position in the write request, starting at 0. For a write that sends `data`, this is the row's position in the `data` array. For a write from a file, this is the row's position among the file's rows.

key.description: The row's key, if it has one.

message.description: A readable explanation of the failure.

state.description: Where the write request stands. `replaced` means that a later replacement of the whole collection ran first, so the collection ends up as if this write ran before the replacement.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

false.description: The component you want to show when your condition is false.

true.description: The component you want to show when your condition is true.

type.description: Defines the widget type.

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the variant. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

body_amp.description: AMP-enabled content for your email. If a recipient's email client doesn't support AMP, they receive your `body` content instead. Make sure you're [set up to send AMP](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/amp-for-email/) first.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

name.description: The name of the variant, if it exists.

newsletter_id.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.

createEmailNewsletter.description: When you create an email, include `subject` and `body`. Set either `from` or `from_id`, but not both. If you set neither, Customer.io uses your oldest verified sending address.

body.description: The HTML body content of the email. Use standard HTML/CSS, not syntax unique to Design Studio.

body_plain.description: The plaintext body of the email. If provided, this overwrites the auto-generated plaintext.

deduped.description: When `true`, Customer.io sends only one message per email address or phone number, even when several profiles share it. Supported on `email`, `twilio`, and `sms` one-time sends. If the send's address is an identifier in your workspace (email for `email` sends, phone number for `twilio` and `sms` sends), Customer.io returns a 422 when you set `deduped` to `true`, because no two profiles can share an identifier and there's nothing to dedupe. Leave it out to use the default for your workspace's identifier configuration. No endpoint changes this later, so set it here if you don't want the default.

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes, so a delayed message doesn't arrive when it's no longer useful. Set it here only alongside `send_now` or `scheduled_at`, because the window runs from the send. On a plain draft, set it on the [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) call instead.

from.description: The address to send the email from, in the format `Name <email@domain.com>`. You can set `from` or `from_id`, but not both. Use one of the `address` values from [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/).

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

layout_id.description: The ID of the [layout](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/3-layouts-and-customerio/) you want to use for the email. If you don't set one, the email uses your workspace's default layout. Find a layout's ID in its URL.

name.description: The name of the one-time send.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

recipient_file_url.description: A URL pointing to a CSV of recipients, used instead of the `recipients` filter. Customer.io resolves the file in the background, so this request can't also send or schedule. Poll [Get a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/getNewsletters/) until `recipient_file_status` is `done`, then call [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/).

recipients.description:
Filter conditions that define the one-time send's recipients. In `recipients`, you can combine `segment` and `attribute` conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not` operators.

This endpoint enforces a strict shape:

* The outermost object must be a single `and` array.
* Every operator or condition object takes exactly **one** key: `and`, `or`, `not`, `segment`, or `attribute`. An object with two keys—like `not` alongside `and`—is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.
* Segment conditions must be wrapped in an `or` array, even for a single segment—and `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.
* To exclude segments, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array.
* Attribute conditions sit directly in the `and` array, unwrapped. To negate an attribute condition, set `inverse: true` on the attribute itself—`not` can't contain attribute conditions.

The email example on this operation shows or-wrapped segments combined with a negated attribute; for the common "include segment A, exclude segment B" pattern, see the **include one segment, exclude another** request example. See [Format API-triggered broadcasts](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-data-format/#overriding-recipients) for general operator behavior.

and.description: An array of conditions that must all be true.

field.description: The attribute name.

inverse.description: Set to `true` for "is not equal" or "does not exist".

operator.description: The comparison operator.

value.description: The value to compare against. Required when `operator` is `eq`.

not.description: A condition or group of conditions to exclude. On this endpoint, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array. An object with both `and` and `not` keys is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.

or.description: An array of conditions where at least one must be true. On this endpoint, `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.

segment.description: A segment condition.

id.description: The ID of a segment.

scheduled_at.description: A Unix timestamp indicating when to send the one-time send. The time must be in the future. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

send_now.description: If `true`, the one-time send is sent immediately after creation. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

subscription_topic_id.description: The one-time send audience's subscription topic ID. Required when [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/#enable-sub-center) is enabled; otherwise sends to globally subscribed profiles.

tag_ids.description: The IDs of the tags you want to apply to the one-time send. Each tag must already exist.

type.description: The channel type for the one-time send.

body_json.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

recipients.description:

This endpoint enforces a strict shape:

oneOf.description: For in-app messages, you must include `body_json`.

body_json.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

last_used.description: The `timestamp` when you last identified this device. If you don't pass a timestamp when you add or update a device, we use the time of the request itself. Our SDKs identify a device when a person launches their app.

disable_message_retention.description: If true, the message body is not retained in delivery history. Setting this value overrides the value set in the settings of your `transactional_message_id`.

drafts.description: If true, your request returns both drafts and active/sent messages.

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the action. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

body_amp.description: AMP-enabled content for your email. If a recipient's email client doesn't support AMP, they receive your `body` content instead. Make sure you're [set up to send AMP](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/amp-for-email/) first.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

deduplicate_id.description: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was updated.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

from.description: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

id.description: The identifier for an action.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

layout.description: The layout used for the action, if it exists.

name.description: The name of the action, if it exists.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

preprocessor.description: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`. Note, Juice replaced Premailer as the pre-processor, but you will only see `premailer` as the value.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

reply_to_id.description: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable. Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

sending_state.description: Determines the sending behavior for the action. `automatic` sends the action automatically when triggered; `draft` queues drafts when the action is triggered; or `off` to disable the action.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

type.description: The type of action.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

email_address.description: The email address of the customer.

action_name.description: The current name of the workflow action identified by action_id, resolved when the event is processed. Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a broadcast.

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

action_name.description: The current name of the workflow action identified by action_id, resolved when the event is processed. Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

oneOf.description: The identifier for an automation.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

action_name.description: The current name of the workflow action identified by action_id, resolved when the event is processed. Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

oneOf.description: The identifier for an automation.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

journey_id.description: The ID for the path a person went through in an automation or API Triggered Broadcast workflow.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

trigger_id.description: The trigger ID returned by the [Trigger Broadcast API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/).

action_name.description: The current name of the workflow action identified by action_id, resolved when the event is processed. Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

oneOf.description: The identifier for an automation.

campaign_tags.description: The tags on the automation, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the automation has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

id.description: A [ULID](https://github.com/ulid/spec) we use to deduplicate events. If an event repeats a value we've already received, we ignore the duplicate. Our Python and Ruby libraries don't pass this ID.

name.description: The screen or deep link path the person viewed, so you can segment your audience or trigger automations from this event. Trim any leading and trailing spaces.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event took place. If you don't provide this value, we use the date-time when we receive the event.

type.description: Indicates that the event represents a mobile screen view. You can also capture screen events directly with [our iOS SDK](/integrations/sdk/ios/track-events/#screen-view-events).

experiment_name.description: The name of the experiment. This value is null if the experiment has no name.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

bulk.description: Set to `true` to process this identify at a lower priority than your other requests. Use it for low-importance updates, like an attribute backfill or a nightly sync from your data warehouse. Customer.io can apply a bulk identify after requests you send later, but the bulk identify never overwrites an attribute that a request with a later `timestamp` set. The field doesn't change message delivery priority. If the identify includes `cio_relationships`, Customer.io deprioritizes only the person's attribute update.

data_file_url.description: The URL of the CSV, GeoJSON, or GeoJSONL file of geofences you want to import. Customer.io reads the file as GeoJSON when its name ends in `.geojson`, `.geojsonl`, or `.json`, or when its content starts with `{`, and as CSV otherwise.

geoset_id.description: The ID of the geofence set you want to import geofences into. The set must already exist in your workspace. Customer.io doesn't check the set when it accepts your request, so a request with an ID that doesn't match a set still succeeds, and the import fails afterward with an error that the geoset doesn't exist. [Look up the import](/integrations/api/app/tag/imports/getImport/) to confirm that it succeeded.

geoset_mode.description: How the import treats geofences that are already in the set. `merge` adds new geofences and updates existing ones. `replace` replaces all the geofences already in the set with the ones you import. In both modes, a geofence with an `external_id` that matches an existing geofence updates that geofence in every set it belongs to.

inAppBodyJson.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

data.description: Contains information about the event, specific to the `object_type` and `metric`.

failure_message.description: Indicates the reason that an attempted message failed.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the reporting webhook event being sent.

metric.description: A message was undeliverable. Undeliverable messages are messages that have either hit a message limit, come from a one-time send that was cancelled or deleted, or an environment that has delivery disabled (which is something you might do if you’re testing an integration). If you’re not using message limits, you probably won’t see this event.

object_type.description: The event relates to an in-app message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

inboxBodyJson.description:
JSON body content for the inbox message, as a stringified JSON object. The fields you include depend on how you [set up your inbox](/journeys/channels/in-app/inbox/setup/):
- `topics`—array, topics your audience can filter by in their inbox
- `type`—string, context that helps render the inbox message
- `properties`—object, your message info like the title, body, link, and image
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days. Otherwise set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit` (`seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, or `days`; relative only), and `value` (number of units, or a unix timestamp if absolute)

action_name.description: The current name of the workflow action identified by action_id, resolved when the event is processed. Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a broadcast.

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

customer_id.description:
The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

object_type.description: The event relates to a notification inbox message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

metric.description: A message was undeliverable. Undeliverable messages are messages that have either hit a message limit, come from a one-time send that was cancelled or deleted, or an environment that has delivery disabled (which is something you might do if you’re testing an integration). If you’re not using message limits, you probably won’t see this event.

object_type.description: The event relates to a notification inbox message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

iosFcmAndApns.description: Your payload changes depending on whether you send to iOS devices through Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) or Apple's Push Notification service (APNs).

message.description: The base object for all FCM payloads.

apns.description: Defines a payload for iOS devices sent through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).

headers.description: Headers defined by [Apple's payload reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/setting_up_a_remote_notification_server/sending_notification_requests_to_apns) that you want to pass through FCM.

push.description: A push payload for the iOS SDK.

body.description: The body of your push notification.

image.description: The URL of an HTTPS image that you want to use for your message.

link.description: A deep link (to a page in your app), or a link to a web page.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

default.description: Whether this is the default variant. Exactly one variant per multi-language message is the default, and it always has an empty `language`.

language.description: The language code for this variant, such as `es` or `fr-CA`. Empty for the default variant—the one that people fall back to when no other variant matches their language.

series.description: Metrics grouped by the requested resolution. Each property is an array where each entry represents one period, such as one day.

clicked.description: The number of `clicked` messages.

created.description: The number of `created` messages.

delivered.description: The number of `delivered` messages.

human_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails excluding machine clicks. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

human_opened.description: The number of `opened` emails excluding machine opens. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

link_untracked.description: The number of emails delivered with link tracking inactive for any reason. We subtract these from the click-rate denominator.

machine_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails attributed to machines—security scanners, bot user agents, known proxy services, and repetitive click patterns. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

open_untracked.description: The number of emails delivered with open tracking inactive for any reason—including the consent opt-outs that `untracked` counts and messages sent with open tracking disabled. We subtract these from the open-rate denominator.

opened.description: The number of `opened` messages.

prefetch_opened.description: The number of `opened` emails attributed to machines. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025.

replied.description: The number of SMS/MMS messages a person replied to with a keyword. [Learn more about inbound messages](/messaging/channels/sms/inbound/get-started/).

spammed.description: The number of spam complaints.

topic_unsubscribed.description: The number of topic unsubscribes in a given period.

tracking_consent_denied.description: The number of people who denied consent to email open tracking in the period.

tracking_consent_granted.description: The number of people who granted consent to email open tracking in the period.

unsubscribed.description: The number of unsubscribes attributed to the automation or message.

untracked.description: The number of `sent` emails whose open pixel we withheld because the person opted out of open tracking. We exclude these from the open-rate denominator; click tracking is unaffected.

languageVariantMetrics.description: Metrics for each language variant of a multi-language message, keyed by the variant's action ID. Only returned when you request metrics for a multi-language branch action.

href.description: The link destination—a URL, mailto, etc.

id.description: The ID of the link.

metric.description: Contains metrics for the link.

clicked.description: An array of results from oldest to newest, where each result indicates a period.

human_clicked.description: An array of human click counts (clicks excluding machine clicks) from oldest to newest, where each result indicates a period. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

machine_clicked.description: An array of machine click counts (clicks attributed to bots or prefetching) from oldest to newest, where each result indicates a period. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

link_id.description: The identifier for the tracked link that a person clicked or tapped.

liveNotificationFreeFormAttributes.description: Your own static fields. On iOS, field names must match the `ActivityAttributes` type in your app. For Android custom types, fields pass through to your app's renderer as-is.
liveNotificationFreeFormAttributes.title: Free-form (iOS or Android custom type)

liveNotificationFreeFormContentState.description: Your own dynamic fields. On iOS, field names must match your `ContentState` type. For Android custom types, fields pass through to your app's renderer as-is. Date fields are epoch seconds.
liveNotificationFreeFormContentState.title: Free-form (iOS or Android custom type)

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

forgotten.description: If true message contents are not retained by Customer.io.

metrics.description: Metrics for an individual instance of a message; each item in the object represents the timestamp when a message achieved a particular metric. This object only contains metrics that have been recorded.

clicked.description: The timestamp when the message was `clicked`.

converted.description: The timestamp when the message was `converted`.

created.description: The timestamp when the message was `created`.

drafted.description: The timestamp when the message was `drafted`.

dropped.description: The timestamp when the message was `dropped`.

human_opened.description: The number of `opened` messages excluding machine opens. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

opened.description: The timestamp when the message was `opened`.

prefetch_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` messages attributed to machines. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025.

prefetch_opened.description: The number of `opened` messages attributed to machines. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025.

sent.description: The timestamp when the message was `sent`.

spammed.description: The timestamp when the message was marked as spam.

undeliverable.description: The timestamp when the message became `undeliverable`.

unsubscribed.description: The timestamp when a person unsubscribed based on this message.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.
