object_type.description: The event relates to an SMS message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

snippet.description: describes a piece of reusable content. You must provide a name for the snippet and the `value`—the content that appears in messages that use the snippet.

name.description: The name of the snippet, must be unique.

updated_at.description: The last date-time the snippet was updated.

value.description: The contents of the snippet.

snippetRequest.description: Request body for creating or updating a snippet. Only `name` and `value` are accepted; `updated_at` is returned in responses only.

name.description: The name of the snippet, must be unique. Trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace before storage.

value.description: The contents of the snippet, in plain text or Liquid. Customer.io trims leading and trailing whitespace before storing it. A snippet can be up to 16,000 characters by default, and all of the snippets in a workspace can total up to 5 MB.

start.description: The unix timestamp representing the beginning of the export.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

subscription_topic_id.description: The identifier of a subscription topic. Remember, subscription topics are assigned an incrementing number, starting at 1.

tags.description: An array of tags you set on this automation.

template_id_event.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

color.description: The color you want to use for this content. You can only set values here that are defined under [**Content** > **In-App Messages**](https://fly.customer.io/env/last/in-app-messages).

maxLines.description: The maximum lines of text you want to display. Text over this limit is controlled by the `overflow` property. If unset, the message displays an unlimited number of lines.

overflow.description: Determines how to handle text that overflows the `maxLines` limit (if set). By default, we cut off overflowing text with ellipsis (`...`).

style.description: The style of text you want to display. You can only set values here that are defined under [**Content** > **In-App Messages**](https://fly.customer.io/env/last/in-app-messages).

text.description: The text you want to display.

textAlign.description: How you want to align this text.

type.description: Defines the widget type.

track-metrics.description: The base properties shared across multiple metric types.

delivery_id.description: The CIO-Delivery-ID from the notification that you want to associate the `event` with.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

tracked.description: If true, Customer.io tracks opens and link clicks in your message.

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the transactional message. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

body_amp.description: AMP-enabled content for your email. If a recipient's email client doesn't support AMP, they receive your `body` content instead. Make sure you're [set up to send AMP](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/amp-for-email/) first.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

from.description: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

id.description: The identifier for an action.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

name.description: The name of the transactional message.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

preprocessor.description: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`. Note, Juice replaced Premailer as the pre-processor, but you will only see `premailer` as the value.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

reply_to_id.description: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable. Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

type.description: The type of message.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

transactionalObject.description: Contains information about a transactional message.

created_at.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

description.description: A description of the transactional message.
description.example: sends a temporary password and lets the customer reset their password.

hide_message_body.description: If true, message contents are not retained in delivery history—you cannot recall the exact contents of the message.

id.description: The identifier Customer.io assigned to the transactional message

link_tracking.description: If true, link tracking is enabled for this message.

name.description: The name you set for the transactional message.

open_tracking.description: If true, open-tracking is enabled for this message.

queue_drafts.description: If true, messages do not send automatically, and queue as drafts instead. You must send drafts through the *Deliveries & Drafts* page in the user interface.

send_to_unsubscribed.description: If true, people with an `unsubscribed` attribute set to `true` can trigger the message.

updated_at.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

attachments.description: A dictionary of attachments where the filename is the key and the value is the base64-encoded contents. The filename must include the extension (i.e. `name.csv`). The base64-encoded contents of all your attachments can total up to 2MB.

bcc.description: Blind copy message recipients. Supports multiple addresses separated by commas. Your request can contain up to 15 total recipients between the `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` keys.

cc.description: Carbon copy message recipients, separated by commas. Unlike BCC recipients, CC recipients are visible to everyone who receives the message. Their opens, clicks, and bounces count toward your message metrics. CC recipients count toward the limit of 15 total recipients across the `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` keys.

disable_css_preprocessing.description: Set to `true` to disable CSS preprocessing. This setting overrides the CSS preprocessing setting on the `transactional_message_id` as set in the user interface. Transactional emails have CSS preprocessing enabled by default.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

headers.description: Custom headers to add to the email, as an object of header names and string values. Names can contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. You can't overwrite reserved headers.

preheader.description: Also known as "preview text", this is the block block of text that users see next to, or underneath, the subject line in their inbox.

reply_to.description: The address that recipients can reply to, if different from the `from` address.

to.description: The recipients you want to send to, separated by commas. You can include up to 15 total recipients across `to`, `cc`, and `bcc`, with optional display names in quotes.

tracked.description: If true, Customer.io tracks opens and link clicks in your message.

disable_message_retention.description: If true, the message body is not retained in delivery history. Setting this value overrides the value set in the settings of your `transactional_message_id`.

identifiers.description: Identifies the person represented by your transactional message by one of, and only one of, `id`, `email`, or `cio_id`.

id.description: The identifier for the person represented by the transactional message. **NOTE**: If your workspace identifies people by email, use the `email` identifier instead.

email.description: The identifier for the person represented by the transactional message. Use this option if your workspace identifies people by email rather than by `id`.

cio_id.description: A unique, immutable identifier for a person, set by Customer.io when you add a person.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

message_data.description: An object containing the key-value pairs referenced using liquid in your message.

queue_draft.description: If true, your transactional message is held as a draft in Customer.io and not sent directly to your audience. You must go to the Deliveries and Drafts page to send your message.

send_at.description: A unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) determining when the message will be sent. The timestamp can be up to 90 days in the future. If this value is in the past, your message is sent immediately.

send_to_unsubscribed.description: If false, your message is not sent to unsubscribed recipients. Setting this value overrides the value set in the settings of your `transactional_message_id`.

custom_data.description: Optional key/value pairs you want to attach to the push payload. Firebase only supports string values. This overrides the Custom Data from your transactional template.

custom_device.description: A device to perform an upsert operation at the time of send. The device will be added/updated on the profile from the Identifiers block.

additionalProperties.description: Custom properties that you want to associate with the device.

attributes.description: Attributes that you can reference to segment your audience—like a person's attributes, but specific to a device. These can be either the attributes defined below or custom key-value attributes.

_last_status.description: The delivery status of the last message sent to the device—sent, bounced, or suppressed. An empty string indicates that that the device hasn't received a push yet.

app_identifier.description: The app that the device belongs to—the **Bundle ID / App identifier** you entered with that app's push credentials. If you have more than one app, we use this attribute to send push notifications to the right app. A device without an app identifier receives push notifications you send to your [default app](/messaging/channels/push/getting-started/#the-default-app).

app_version.description: The version of your app that a customer uses. You might target app versions to let people know when they need to update, or expose them to new features when they do.

cio_sdk_version.description: The version of the Customer.io SDK in the app.

device_locale.description: The device's [IETF language code](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started/#supported-languages), such as `en-MX` or `es-ES`.

device_model.description: The model of the device a person uses.

device_os.description: The operating system, including the version, on the device.

push_enabled.description: If `"true"`, the device is opted-in and can receive push notifications.

last_used.description: The `timestamp` when you last identified this device. If you don't pass a timestamp when you add or update a device, we use the time of the request itself. Our SDKs identify a device when a person launches their app.

custom_payload.description: Optional key/value pairs you want to attach to the push payload. Firebase only supports string values. This overrides all other payload values, including the Custom Payload from your transactional template.

android.description: A custom push payload for Android devices.

message.description: The parent object for Android custom push payloads.

android.description: Contains custom push options for your notification.

notification.description: Properties supported specifically by Android on FCM.

body_loc_arg.description: Variable string values used in place of the format specifiers in `body_loc_key` to localize the body text to the user's current localization. See Formatting and Styling for more information.

body_loc_key.description: String resource key used to localize the body text. See Android [String resources](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/string-resource/).

click_action.description: The action that occurs when a user taps on the notification. Launches an activity with a matching intent filter when a person taps the notification.

color.description: The notification's icon color in `#rrggbb` format.

icon.description: Sets the notification icon to `myicon` for drawable resource `myicon`. If you don't send this key, FCM displays the launcher icon from your app manifest.

sound.description: The sound that plays when the device receives the notification. Supports `"default"` or the filename of a sound resource bundled in your app. Sound files must reside in `/res/raw/`.

tag.description: An identifier you use to replace an existing notification. If a notification with the same tag is already showing, the new one replaces it. Leave it empty to create a new notification each time.

title_loc_arg.description: Variable string values used in place of the format specifiers in `title_loc_key` to localize the title text to the user's current localization. See Formatting and Styling for more information.

title_loc_key.description: String resource key used to localize the title text. See Android [String resources](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/string-resource/).

data.description: Contains key-value pairs that your app interprets.

notification.description: Contains the push body and title.

body.description: The body of your push notification.

title.description: The title of your push notification.

ios.description: Your payload changes depending on whether you send to iOS devices through Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) or Apple's Push Notification service (APNs).

message.description: The base object for all FCM payloads.

apns.description: Defines a payload for iOS devices sent through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).

headers.description: Headers defined by [Apple's payload reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/setting_up_a_remote_notification_server/sending_notification_requests_to_apns) that you want to pass through FCM.

additionalProperties.description: Additional properties that you've set up your app to interpret outside of the Customer.io SDK.

CIO.description: Contains properties interpreted by the Customer.io iOS SDK.

push.description: A push payload for the iOS SDK.

body.description: The body of your push notification.

image.description: The URL of an HTTPS image that you want to use for your message.

link.description: A deep link (to a page in your app), or a link to a web page.

title.description: The title of your push notification.

aps.description: A push payload intended for an iOS device.

oneOf.description: A simple alert message.
oneOf.title: Simple alert

body.description: The body of your push notification.

launch-image.description: The name of the launch image file you want to display. When a user launches your app, they'll see this image or storyboard file rather than your app’s normal launch image.

loc-args.description: An array of replacement value strings for variables in your message text. Each %@ character in the loc-key is replaced by a value from this array, in the order they appear in the message body.

loc-key.description: The key for a localized message string in your app’s Localizable.strings file.

subtitle.description: Additional information that explains the purpose of the notification.

subtitle-loc-args.description: An array of replacement value strings for variables in your subtitle string. Each %@ character in the subtitle-loc-key is replaced by a value from this array, in the order they appear in the subtitle string.

subtitle-loc-key.description: The key for a localized subtitle string in your app’s Localizable.strings file.

title.description: The title of your push notification.

title-loc-args.description: An array of replacement value strings for variables in your title string. Each %@ character in the title-loc-key is replaced by a value from this array, in the order they appear in the title string.

title-loc-key.description: The key for a localized title string in your app’s Localizable.strings files.

badge.description: The number you want to display on your app's icon. Set to 0 to remove the current badge, if any.

category.description: The notification’s type. This string must correspond to the identifier of one of the `UNNotificationCategory` objects you register at launch time.

content-available.description: The background notification flag. Use `1` without an `alert` to perform a silent update. `0` indicates a normal push notification.

interruption-level.description: Indicates the importance and delivery timing of a notification.

mutable-content.description: Set this to `1` if you use the Customer.io SDK, so you can support images and delivered metrics in your push notifications. It passes the notification to your service extension before delivery.

relevance-score.description: A number between 0 and 1. The highest score is considered the "most relevant"  and is featured in the notification summary.

oneOf.description: The name of a sound file in your app’s main bundle or in the Library/Sounds folder of your app’s container directory. Use “default” to play the system sound. For critical alerts, you'll pass an object instead.
oneOf.title: Regular alert

name.description: The name of a sound file in your app’s main bundle or in the Library/Sounds folder of your app’s container directory. Use “default” to play the system sound.

volume.description: The volume for a critical alert between 0 and 1, where 0 is silent and 1 is full volume.

target-content-id.description: The identifier of the window brought forward.

thread-id.description: An identifier to group related notifications.

language.description: Overrides language preferences for the person you want to send your transactional message to. Use one of our [supported two- or four-letter language codes](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started/#supported-languages).

link.description: A deep link to open when the push is tapped. This overrides Link from the transactional template (referenced by `transactional_message_id`).

message.description: The message body for your notification. This overrides the notification body of the transactional template (referenced by `transactional_message_id`).

platform.description: The devices this send goes to, overriding the platform saved on the transactional message for this request only. `all` is iOS and Android, `web` is browsers only, and `all_and_web` is iOS, Android, and browsers. If you leave it out, the send uses the message's platform; with `auto_create`, a new message keeps the platform of its first request. Values other than `all` require [web push](/messaging/channels/web-push/transactional/) for your account; without it, the request fails with `400`.

sound.description: **For iOS Only**: your notification can alert users with the device's default notification sound or play no sound at all.

title.description: The title for your notification. This overrides the title of the transactional template (referenced by `transactional_message_id`).

to.description: The devices you want to send this push to—`all`, `last_used`, or a custom device token from the identified profile. Defaults to `all` and overrides the `To` value from your transactional template.

triggerFilter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment, attribute, and device attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

field.description: The name of the attribute you want to filter against.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* meet the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

device_attribute.description: Filter your audience by the devices people have. We match a person if any of their devices meets the condition. To match people who have any device at all, set `field` to `id` and `operator` to `exists`.

field.description: The name of the device attribute you want to filter against. Use `id` to match people who have a device.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* have a device meeting the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute; `eq` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this device attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

not.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *aren't* in the segment.

v1_cio_relationships.description: Describes relationships to an entity—a non-person object in Customer.io, like a company, educational course, job board, etc.

action.description: This determines whether the `relationships` array adds relationships to a person or removes them from a person.

relationships.description: Each object in the array represents a relationship you want to add to, or remove from, a person.

identifiers.description: The identifiers for a particular object. You can use either the `object_type_id` and `object_id` (where `object_type_id` represents the type of object and the `object_id` is the individual identifier for the object) or the `cio_object_id`.

object_id.description: The unique identifier for an object. If you use an `object_id` that already exists, we'll update the object accordingly.

object_type_id.description: The object type an object belongs to—like "Companies" or "Accounts". Object type IDs are string-formatted integers that begin at `1` and increment for each new type.

cio_object_id.description: A unique value that Customer.io sets for an object when you create it. This ID is immutable.

relationship_attributes.description: The attributes associated with a relationship. Passing null or an empty string removes the attribute from the relationship.

v2_cio_relationships.description: The people you want to associate with an object. Each object in the array represents a person.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

relationship_attributes.description: The attributes associated with a relationship. Passing null or an empty string removes the attribute from the relationship.

variables_event.description: User-defined variables associated with the message, as key-value pairs. This key only appears if you enabled the **Body content** option (`with_content` in the App API) when setting up your webhook and the delivery has variables.

variant_id.description: The identifier of a one-time send variant—a language in a multi-language one-time send or a test in an A/B test.

body.description: The body of the action. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

layout.description: The layout used for the action, if it exists.

method.description: The HTTP method for your webhook.

name.description: The name of the action, if it exists.

sending_state.description: Determines the sending behavior for the action. `automatic` sends the action automatically when triggered; `draft` queues drafts when the action is triggered; or `off` to disable the action.

type.description: The type of action.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

url.description: The URL to send a webhook to, applies to `webhook` type actions.

Omitted when the name isn't available, including when the action was deleted. For A/B splits, action_id is the selected variant sub-action, so action_name names that variant—the same value the legacy webhook's message_name carries. parent_action_id carries the split.

broadcast_name.description: The name of the broadcast. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the broadcast was deleted.

broadcast_tags.description: The tags on the broadcast, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the broadcast has no tags or the tags aren't available.

The ID of the person the webhook event occurred to. Blank if the person in question has been deleted.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

While webhooks may still contain this property, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` object wherever possible.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

data.description: Contains information about the event, specific to the `object_type` and `metric`.

content.description: The stringified payload sent to your webhook address. This key only appears if you enabled the **Body content** option (`with_content` in the App API) when setting up your webhook.

recipient.description: The URL the webhook was sent to.

variables.description: User-defined variables associated with the message, as key-value pairs. This key only appears if you enabled the **Body content** option (`with_content` in the App API) when setting up your webhook and the delivery has variables.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the reporting webhook event being sent.

metric.description: A webhook was sent from Customer.io. If you enabled the **Body content** option (`with_content` in the App API) with your webhook, the payload includes the `content` of your webhook.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

whatsAppActionObject.description: The action object for WhatsApp messages sent from Customer.io using your Facebook Business Account (not Twilio). Messages sent through Twilio still use the `twilio` type and are treated similarly to SMS messages.

body.description: A JSON string containing WhatsApp template metadata from Meta and template parameters with Liquid variables. Use `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/whatsapp/templates` to list templates.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

deduplicate_id.description: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was updated.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

name.description: The name of the action.

recipient.description: The recipient's phone number in E.164 format, usually referenced with Liquid like `{{customer.phone}}`. If you use Liquid, this field is blank in `GET` responses because we resolve the recipient at send time.

send_to_unsubscribed.description: Whether to send this message to unsubscribed customers.

sender_identity_id.description:
The ID of the WhatsApp Business phone number to send from. This corresponds to
a phone number registered in your WhatsApp Business Account and synced via
`GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/whatsapp/sync`.

sending_state.description: Determines the sending behavior for the action. `automatic` sends the action automatically when triggered; `draft` queues drafts when the action is triggered; or `off` to disable the action.

tracked.description: Whether links in template parameters should be tracked.

type.description: For WhatsApp messages sent from Customer.io using your Facebook Business Account (not Twilio), the `type` is always `whatsapp`.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

identifiers.description:
The person the event represents. This object contains all of the identifiers enabled in your workspace, even if they aren't set for the person. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.

cio_id.description: The canonical identifier for a person, present only if your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID). This value exists to keep a record of a person in your workspace across changes to their other identifiers.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

phone.description: The person's phone number. This key only appears if your workspace has phone enabled as an identifier.

oneOf.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

newsletter_name.description: The name of the one-time send. Omitted when the name isn't available—for example, if the one-time send was deleted.

newsletter_tags.description: The tags on the one-time send, as an array of tag names. Omitted when the one-time send has no tags or the tags aren't available.

template_id.description: The ID of the template used to render the message. A message's content can change over its lifetime; this is the template used for this delivery. For one-time sends (newsletters), this matches `content_id`.

data.description: Contains information about the event, specific to the `object_type` and `metric`.

failure_message.description: Indicates the reason that an attempted message failed.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the reporting webhook event being sent.

metric.description: A message was undeliverable. Undeliverable messages are messages that have either hit a message limit, come from a one-time send that was cancelled or deleted, or an environment that has delivery disabled (which is something you might do if you're testing an integration). If you're not using message limits, you probably won't see this event.

object_type.description: The event relates to a WhatsApp message.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event occurred.

widgetColor.description: The color you want to use for this content. You can only set values here that are defined under [**Content** > **In-App Messages**](https://fly.customer.io/env/last/in-app-messages).

widgetComponents.description: An array of child components that you want to make available inside this widget.

widgetCrossAxisAlignment.description: The crossAxisAlignment property supports the following options

widgetHeight.description: The height of the component in pixels, if you want to constrain it. If you don't set a height or width, we'll scale your content to fit your message or container.

widgetMainAxisAlignment.description: The mainAxisAlignment property supports the following options.

widgetRadius.description: Sets the radius of corners for an item in pixels, similar to the `border-radius` CSS property.

widgetWidth.description: The width of the component in pixels, if you want to constrain it. If you don't set a height or width, we'll scale your content to fit your message or container.

workspace.description: Contains workspace properties including the count of messages, people, and objects. Customer.io caches these counts, so your data may be up to two hours old.

billable_messages_sent.description: The count of [emails sent](/journeys/channels/message-statuses/#sent) that are considered for billing in your current billing period. Ultimately, we only bill for the overages on your plan.

id.description: The id of the workspace.

messages_sent.description: The count of [messages sent](/journeys/channels/message-statuses/#sent) via any channel (email, SMS, in-app, push, slack) in the current billing period.

name.description: The name of the workspace.

object_types.description: The current count of object types in the workspace. Updates roughly every hour.

objects.description: The current count of object profiles in the workspace. Updates roughly every hour.

people.description: The current count of people profiles in the workspace. Updates roughly every hour.

Bearer-Auth.description:
The App API uses a bearer authentication scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Use a **private key** (`sk_`) from the [API Credentials page](https://fly.customer.io/settings/api_credentials?keyType=app). Legacy App API keys also work. [Learn more about public and private keys](/accounts/settings/managing-credentials/#public-and-private-keys).

ServiceAccount-Auth.description:
Transactional send endpoints (`/v1/send/email`, `/v1/send/push`, `/v1/send/sms`, `/v1/send/whatsapp`, `/v1/send/in_app`, `/v1/send/inbox_message`) also accept a service-account bearer token, prefixed with `sa_live_`. Service-account tokens work across workspaces, so you must pass the target workspace as the `X-Workspace-Id` header on each request.

Service-account tokens are intended for testing and one-off sends—for example, using the Customer.io CLI with an AI agent like Claude to verify that a transactional message renders correctly before wiring it into your production backend. **For the production integration that triggers the message from your application, use a private key instead**: it's workspace-scoped, easier to rotate, and has a smaller blast radius.

Service-account tokens are server-side credentials. Treat them like any API key—keep them in environment variables or a secret manager, and never embed them in client-side code, mobile apps, or other untrusted contexts.

bearerAuth.description: API key passed as a Bearer token.

info.description: Our App API provides ways to trigger messages and retrieve information about people, automations, broadcasts, and more. # Overview The App API provides methods to send newsletters, transactional messages, and API-triggered broadcasts. You can create newsletters from scratch and update transactional messages and API-triggered broadcasts. For transactional messages and API-triggered broadcasts, your payload acts as a message "trigger" and can contain `data` that you reference in your messages using liquid—`{{trigger.}}`. The other endpoints help you retrieve information about people, segments, automations, broadcasts, etc; it also lets you update automation actions, messages, newsletter variants, etc. Aside from the [API-triggered broadcast](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/) endpoint (1 per 10 seconds for each workspace), requests are limited to 10 per second. [Transactional](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendEmail/) messages aren't rate limited. # We may add to these APIs As we release new features, we add endpoints and we may even add fields to existing endpoints. We don't announce these additions in advance. Fields we add will be backward compatible: existing fields keep their names and types. Build your integration to ignore fields it doesn't recognize. If you validate responses against a schema, make sure the schema accepts unknown keys. In JSON Schema, for example, don't set `additionalProperties: false`. # Use our Postman collection We've generated a Postman collection to help you get started with our APIs. If you fork this collection, you might want to disable the *Watch original collection* option. We automatically update our Postman collection whenever we release changes to our documentation, even if we don't change our APIs—which happens daily! Rather than being flooded with Postman notifications, you can check out our [Release Notes](/release-notes/) for updates to our APIs. **NOTE**: Postman endpoints default to our US APIs. If you're in our European (EU) region, you'll need to add `-eu` to the server variables (`track_api_url` and `app_api_url`). [](https://god.gw.postman.com/run-collection/23697545-2931c004-e63d-4cdc-bf4b-e685ba6da42d?action=collection%2Ffork&source=rip_markdown&collection-url=entityId%3D23697545-2931c004-e63d-4cdc-bf4b-e685ba6da42d%26entityType%3Dcollection%26workspaceId%3Db886877f-fc09-475f-84fe-6221a98f4d18#?env%5BCustomer.io%20API%20Environment%) # Server addresses: US and EU Customer.io hosts services in the United States (US) and European Union. Select the appropriate server address for your region. | Region | Server Address | | :-- | :-- | | US | https://api.customer.io | | EU | https://api-eu.customer.io | # Authentication All requests to the Customer.io App API use a private key (`sk_`) as a bearer token in the HTTP `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer `. Create a private key on the [API Credentials page](https://fly.customer.io/settings/api_credentials?keyType=app). [Learn more about public and private keys](/accounts/settings/managing-credentials/#public-and-private-keys). If you already use an App API key, you can keep using it with bearer authentication. # Rate Limits Most endpoints on this page are limited to 10 requests per second. The exceptions are: * [Transactional messages](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendEmail/) aren't rate limited. * The [API-triggered broadcast endpoint](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/) is limited to 1 request every 10 seconds across all the broadcasts in a workspace. If you need to trigger broadcasts more often, contact us to talk through your use case. **Rate limits are subject to change. We may adjust these thresholds to ensure stable performance for all customers.**

get.description:
Returns account-wide activity: sign-ins and failed sign-ins, team members, roles, API keys, and single sign-on (SSO) settings.

This endpoint requires an [audit log key](/accounts/audit-logs/#get-audit-logs-through-the-api). It works only while the team member who created the key is an account admin. Other App API keys return a `403`.

Entries include the IP address of each change and the email address of each team member named. Results cover the audit log history your plan includes.

parameters.description: The number of entries to return, up to 100. If you ask for more, you get 100.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The order of the results. `desc` returns the newest entries first. Use `asc` to poll for new entries: pass the `id` of the last entry you received as `cursor` to get only the entries after it.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: An audit log entry `id`. Returns the entries after it when `sort_order=asc`, or before it when `sort_order=desc`. Pass the `next_cursor` from your previous response to get the next page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Returns entries at or after this time, in RFC 3339 format, like `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`. If the time is earlier than your plan's audit log history, results start at the earliest entry your plan includes.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: Returns entries at or before this time, in RFC 3339 format.
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: Returns entries for actions taken by this team member.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.name: service_account_id

parameters.description: Returns entries from IP addresses that start with this value.
parameters.name: ip_addr

parameters.description: Returns entries for one kind of object, using the names in the `object_type` field of each entry, like `Segment` or `User`.
parameters.name: object_type

parameters.description: Returns entries for one object. Requires `object_type`.
parameters.name: object_id

parameters.description: Returns entries for one kind of change. Requires `object_type` or `object_id`.
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: Returns entries where this field changed. Requires `object_type` or `object_id`.
parameters.name: attribute_name

data.description: The audit log entries.

account_id.description: The account the change belongs to. `0` on workspace audit log entries, which belong to the workspace your key is for.

action.description: The kind of change, like `Created`, `Updated`, or `Deleted`.

changed_from.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, before the change.

changed_to.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, after the change.

data.description: The object as it was saved after the change. The shape depends on `object_type`. A `FailedLogin` entry carries `login_method`, `reason` (like `invalid_password` or `invalid_2fa_code`), and `user_agent`.

id.description: The entry's identifier. Use it as a `cursor` to page through results.

meta.description: Request details recorded with the change.

object_id.description: The identifier of the object that changed. For a `FailedLogin` entry, this is the team member whose sign-in failed.

object_type.description: The kind of object that changed, like `Segment`, `User`, or `FailedLogin`.

Each has its own `changed_from` and `changed_to`, so you can see the segment's rules as they were at the time.

For objects that keep one, like segments and automations, it generally goes up as the object changes, but some updates don't change it, so use `id` to put an object's entries in order. The value is `0` on entries that don't record a version.

limit.description: The number of entries per page. If you asked for more than 100, this is 100.

next_cursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` to get the next page. `0` on the last page, which can still hold entries.

name.description: The service account's name.

users.description: The team members named in `data`, with their email addresses.

deleted.description: Whether the team member was removed from the account.

email.description: The team member's email address.

user_id.description: The team member's ID.

get.description: This endpoint returns a list of "activities" for people, similar to your workspace's Activity Logs. This endpoint is guaranteed to return activity history within the past 30 days. It _might_ return data older than 30 days in some circumstances, but activites older than 30 days are not guaranteed.

parameters.description: The token for the page of results you want to return. Responses contain a `next` property. Use this property as the `start` value to return the next page of results.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The type of activity you want to search for. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.
parameters.name: type

schema.description: The type of activity. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

parameters.description: The name of the event or attribute you want to return. For `consent` activities, the consent action, like `opted_in` or `opted_out`.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: If true, return results for deleted people.
parameters.name: deleted

parameters.description:
The `identifier` of the person you want to look up. By default, this is a person's `id`. You can use the `id_type` parameter to look up a person by `email`, `phone`, or `cio_id`.

If you use a person's `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_` when using it to find or reference a person (i.e. `cio_03000010` for a `cio_id` value of 03000010).
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: The type of `customer_id` you want to use to reference a person. If you don't provide this parameter, we assume that the `customer_id` in your request is a person's `id`. You can use `email` and `phone` only if they're enabled as identifiers in your [workspace settings](/accounts/workspaces/overview/#migrate-workspace); otherwise the request returns `400`. Reference `phone` values in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164), like `+14155552671`, and URL-encode the leading `+` as `%2B`.
parameters.name: id_type

parameters.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.
parameters.name: limit

customer_id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

customer_identifiers.description: Identifiers for the person in a response—`id`, `cio_id`, and `email`. Unset `id` or `email` values are `null`. We recommend this object over the less descriptive `customer_id`. This object doesn't include `phone`, even if your workspace uses phone numbers as an identifier; look for the person's `phone` attribute instead.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

email.description: A person's email address, if set.

id.description: A person's unique ID, if set. This is the same as the `customer_id` if present.

delivered.description: The date-time when the message was delivered, if applicable.

delivery_id.description: The message ID.

opened.description: Indicates whether or not a customer opened a message, if the message was delivered.

from.description: The old attribute value. If empty, the customer probably didn't bear the attribute before this action.

oneOf.description: The name of the object is the attribute that changed.
oneOf.title: Attribute change

oneOf.description: The data for a `consent` activity. The activity's `name` is the action, `opted_in` or `opted_out`. Customer.io fills in the optional fields when the change that created the record has that information. See [Consent records](/messaging/channels/subscriptions/consent-records/#what-a-record-contains).

channel.description: The channel the consent applies to, like `email` or `sms`. Absent when the consent applies to all of your messages.

collection_point.description: Where the change came from, like your subscription center or an SMS reply. The `subscription_preference_migration` and `sender_optout_migration` values mark records that Customer.io imported from preferences and opt-outs that existed before your account recorded consent.

consent_state.description: The state the change left the person in.

delivery_id.description: The message the person responded to, like the email that contained the unsubscribe link.

from.description: The sender's email address or phone number when the change happened.

profile_identifier.description: The identifier your request used to find the person.

received_on.description: The address or phone number the person's reply came from.

response.description: What the person sent back, like the body of an SMS reply.

sender_id.description: The sender identity the consent applies to, if any.

source_event_id.description: The ID of the activity that produced this record, like the inbound SMS that contained STOP.

topic_id.description: The subscription topic the consent applies to, if any.

topic_name.description: The topic's name when the change happened. Renaming the topic later doesn't change this value.

id.description: The identifier for the action.

name.description: The name of the event, for `event` and `screen` activities. For `consent` activities, the consent action, which is `opted_in`, `opted_out`, or `voided`.

get.description:
Returns the activity in the workspace your key belongs to, like changes to automations, segments, and imports. To collect logs from several workspaces, use a key from each one.

This endpoint works with a private key or an [audit log key](/accounts/audit-logs/#get-audit-logs-through-the-api). Entries include the IP address of each change and the email address of each team member named. Results cover the audit log history your plan includes.

On large workspaces, filter by `object_type` and page with `cursor` rather than raising `limit`.

parameters.description: The number of entries to return, up to 100. If you ask for more, you get 100.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The order of the results. `desc` returns the newest entries first. Use `asc` to poll for new entries: pass the `id` of the last entry you received as `cursor` to get only the entries after it.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: An audit log entry `id`. Returns the entries after it when `sort_order=asc`, or before it when `sort_order=desc`. Pass the `next_cursor` from your previous response to get the next page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Returns entries at or after this time, in RFC 3339 format, like `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`. If the time is earlier than your plan's audit log history, results start at the earliest entry your plan includes.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: Returns entries at or before this time, in RFC 3339 format.
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: Returns entries for actions taken by this team member.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: Returns entries for actions taken by this service account.
parameters.name: service_account_id

parameters.description: Returns entries from IP addresses that start with this value.
parameters.name: ip_addr

parameters.description: Returns entries for one kind of object, using the names in the `object_type` field of each entry, like `Segment` or `User`.
parameters.name: object_type

parameters.description: Returns entries for one object. Requires `object_type`.
parameters.name: object_id

parameters.description: Returns entries for one kind of change. Requires `object_type` or `object_id`.
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: Returns entries where this field changed. Requires `object_type` or `object_id`.
parameters.name: attribute_name

parameters.description: Returns entries for the actions in one automation. Requires `object_type=CampaignAction`.
parameters.name: campaign_id

parameters.description: Returns only API-triggered broadcasts, or excludes them. Requires `object_type=Campaign`.
parameters.name: campaign_type

data.description: The audit log entries.

account_id.description: The account the change belongs to. `0` on workspace audit log entries, which belong to the workspace your key is for.

action.description: The kind of change, like `Created`, `Updated`, or `Deleted`.

changed_from.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, before the change.

changed_to.description: For an update, the values of the fields that changed, after the change.

data.description: The object as it was saved after the change. The shape depends on `object_type`. A `FailedLogin` entry carries `login_method`, `reason` (like `invalid_password` or `invalid_2fa_code`), and `user_agent`.

id.description: The entry's identifier. Use it as a `cursor` to page through results.

ip_addr.description: The IP address the change came from.

meta.description: Request details recorded with the change.

object_id.description: The identifier of the object that changed. For a `FailedLogin` entry, this is the team member whose sign-in failed.

object_type.description: The kind of object that changed, like `Segment`, `User`, or `FailedLogin`.

related_logs.description: On a `Segment` entry, the latest `Condition` entry for each of the segment's conditions, and the latest `EventType` entry for each event those conditions name, from before the segment changed. Each has its own `changed_from` and `changed_to`, so you can see the segment's rules as they were at the time.

service_account_id.description: The service account that made the change, if any.

timestamp.description: When the change happened, as a unix timestamp in seconds.

user_id.description: The team member who made the change, matching a `user_id` in the response's `users` array. `0` when no signed-in team member made the change, like a failed sign-in.

version.description: The object's version number after the change. For objects that keep one, like segments and automations, it generally goes up as the object changes, but some updates don't change it, so use `id` to put an object's entries in order. The value is `0` on entries that don't record a version.

limit.description: The number of entries per page. If you asked for more than 100, this is 100.

next_cursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` to get the next page. `0` on the last page, which can still hold entries.

deleted.description: Whether the service account was deleted.

name.description: The service account's name.

users.description: The team members named in `data`, with their email addresses.

deleted.description: Whether the team member was removed from the account.

email.description: The team member's email address.

user_id.description: The team member's ID.

200.description: A page of workspace audit log entries.

400.description: A parameter is invalid, like a `start_time` that isn't in RFC 3339 format or an `object_type` that isn't a workspace activity.

403.description: The key doesn't have access to the workspace audit log.

get.description:
Returns the actions that occur as a part of a broadcast.

If a message block contains multiple languages, this endpoint returns an object for each language variant. Each language variant includes the `multi_language_branch_action_id` property with the same value. Use this id to retrieve metrics for each language variant in a single request through [Get broadcast action metrics](/integrations/api/app/tag/broadcasts/broadcastActionMetrics/).

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the action. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

body_amp.description: AMP-enabled content for your email. If a recipient's email client doesn't support AMP, they receive your `body` content instead. Make sure you're [set up to send AMP](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/amp-for-email/) first.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

from.description: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

headers.description: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`. Names and values must be strings, with no non-ASCII characters or spaces. You can't overwrite reserved headers.

id.description: The identifier for an action.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

layout.description: The layout used for the action, if it exists.

multi_language_branch_action_id.description: Returned when the action is a language variant of a multi-language message. This id is the same for each variant of a message, so you can use this to retrieve metrics for a message and all its variants.

name.description: The name of the action, if it exists.

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

preprocessor.description: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`. Note, Juice replaced Premailer as the pre-processor, but you will only see `premailer` as the value.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

reply_to_id.description: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable. Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

sending_state.description: Determines the sending behavior for the action. `automatic` sends the action automatically when triggered; `draft` queues drafts when the action is triggered; or `off` to disable the action.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

get.description:
Returns a list of metrics for an individual action both in total and in `steps` (days, weeks, etc) over a period of time. Stepped `series` metrics return from oldest to newest (i.e. the 0-index for any result is the oldest step/period).

You cannot request fewer than 2 steps of any period (2 hours, 2 days, 2 weeks, or 2 months). For instance, `?period=days&steps=1` means two days - the 48 hours before the API request was made. `?period=days&steps=0` returns the same as the maximum of the period - `?period=days&steps=45`. See the `steps` parameter below for the maximum count of each period.

**Multi-language messages**

If the action is a [multi-language](/messaging/channels/localization/getting-started/) message, you can retrieve metrics for a single language variant or all language variants. To retrieve metrics for a single language variant, pass the `id` of the action. To retrieve aggregate metrics and a breakdown for each language variant, pass the `multi_language_branch_action_id`, which is the same for each variant of a message. You can get both ids from the [List broadcast actions](/integrations/api/app/tag/broadcasts/broadcastActions/) endpoint.

If you pass the `multi_language_branch_action_id`, then the `metric` object shows the *total* across every variant. The `language_variants` object shows a breakdown for each language variant.

If you want to get the sum of all metrics across all of a broadcast's actions, you can use each action id of a multi-language message, like you would for other types of actions.

get.description:
Returns information about the deliveries (instances of messages sent to individual people) sent from an API-triggered broadcast. Provide query parameters to refine the metrics you want to return.

Use the `start_ts` and `end_ts` to find messages within a time range. If your request doesn't include `start_ts` and `end_ts` parameters, we'll return results for the 1 month period after the first trigger. If your `start_ts` and `end_ts` range is more than 6 months, we'll return 6 months of data from the most recent timestamp in your request. Timestamps reflect when deliveries were created in our system, not when they were actually sent to recipients. There may be a delay between creation and sending.

post.description:
Trigger a broadcast and optionally provide data to populate liquid placeholders in the message. To trigger one-time send broadcasts, use the [one-time send endpoint](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/).

Broadcasts are optimized to send messages to a large audience and not for one-to-one interactions. Use our [transactional API](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendEmail/) or [event-triggered automations](/journeys/send/campaigns/triggers/#event-trigger) to respond to your audience on an individual, one-to-one basis.

**Define your audience**

**The shape of the request depends on how you define your audience**: default (the recipients set in the UI), custom conditions, a list of emails, a list of customer IDs, a map of users, or a data file.

You can narrow any of these audiences, except the default audience, with the `filter` object. This is useful when a file or a list of people is broader than the audience you want for your broadcast.

**You can only trigger broadcasts to send to people you've already added to your workspace.** A broadcast cannot add or identify new people. If you reference people who don't exist in your broadcast audience, the broadcast will fail by default. You can override this behavior by setting the `email_ignore_missing` and/or `id_ignore_missing` flags to `true`. The broadcast will skip over any people who don't exist in your workspace and send to the remaining recipients.

You can reference properties in the `data` object in your broadcast using liquid—`{{trigger.<property_in_data_obj>}}`.

**Send or schedule your broadcast**

By default, we send your broadcast as soon as you trigger it. Set `scheduled_at` to send it at a future time instead. You can [cancel the trigger](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/cancelBroadcastTrigger/) to stop a scheduled send before it starts sending. You can't change a trigger's `scheduled_at` value later; if you need to reschedule your broadcast, you must cancel the trigger and re-trigger the broadcast with the new timestamp.

If your broadcast produces a `422` error, you can [get more information about the errors](/integrations/api/app/tag/broadcasts/broadcastErrors/) to see what went wrong.

**Limits**

You can send 1 trigger request every 10 seconds. The limit covers all the broadcasts in your workspace, so triggering two different broadcasts within 10 seconds also returns a `429`. Each broadcast can have up to 5 [queued](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#what-does-queueing-mean) triggers at a time. If you need to trigger broadcasts more often, contact us to talk through your use case.

A broadcast can send to everyone in its audience, with no limit on the number of people, when you use the broadcast's default audience, a `recipients` filter, or a `data_file_url` file. If you define recipients manually with `ids`, `emails`, or `per_user_data`, you can include up to 10,000 people in each request. Each trigger request can be up to 25MB.

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

filter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment, attribute, and device attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

field.description: The name of the attribute you want to filter against.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* meet the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

device_attribute.description: Filter your audience by the devices people have. We match a person if any of their devices meets the condition. To match people who have any device at all, set `field` to `id` and `operator` to `exists`.

field.description: The name of the device attribute you want to filter against. Use `id` to match people who have a device.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* have a device meeting the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute; `eq` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this device attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

device_attribute.title: device attribute

not.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

anyOf.description: Filter for people who belong to a segment.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

recipients.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment and attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

recipients.title: Audience Filter

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: Custom recipients

oneOf.description: An array of emails you want to send the broadcast to. These addresses must already exist; your request cannot create a new person.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

emails.description: An array of email addresses you want to send the broadcast to. These addresses must already exist; your request cannot create a new person. You can list up to 10,000 emails in this field. To send to a larger audience, use `recipients` or `data_file_url`, which don't limit the size of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: Emails

oneOf.description: An array of customer ids that you want to send the broadcast to. These IDs must already exist; your request cannot create a new person.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.
