id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

ids.description: An array of IDs you want to send a broadcast to. To send to a larger audience, define it with `recipients` or `data_file_url` instead. **NOTE**: If your workspace identifies people by `email`, don't use this option. Identify your audience by `emails` instead.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: IDs

oneOf.description: An array of JSON objects containing `id` or `email` keys and a `data` key. Each object represents a person you want to send the broadcast to and data you want to personalize their message with using liquid.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

per_user_data.description: The people you want to send a broadcast to, with custom data to personalize each message. Each person must already exist in your workspace—a broadcast trigger can't create people. Each entry can be up to 2MB. To personalize messages for a larger audience, use `data_file_url` instead.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Merge data associated with the recipient.

id.description: The ID of the recipient.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Merge data associated with the recipient.

email.description: The email address of the recipient. This address must be unique in your workspace. If more than one person has the same `email` attribute, your request will produce an error.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

oneOf.title: User Maps

oneOf.description: The URL of a data file with one JSON object per line, using either `id` and `data` or `email` and `data`. The people you reference must already exist in your workspace. The file may be gzip-compressed to reduce transfer size (recommended for large files); if compressed, it must use gzip and the hosting server must return a `Content-Encoding` header set to `gzip` when the file is downloaded.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in your message here.

data.description: Contains information you want to use to populate your broadcast. The `data` object can be up to 50KB. If you need more personalization data, you can send it per person with `per_user_data` or `data_file_url`.

example.headline: Roadrunner spotted in Albuquerque!
example.text: We received reports of a roadrunner in your immediate area! Head to your dashboard to view more information!

data_file_url.description: The URL of a JSON Lines file with one person per line, using `id` and `data` or `email` and `data`. The people you reference must already exist in your workspace. The file can be up to 10GB, and each line can be up to 2MB. The file may be gzip-compressed to reduce transfer size (recommended for large files); if compressed, it must use gzip and the hosting server must return a `Content-Encoding` header set to `gzip` when the file is downloaded.

email_add_duplicates.description: an email address associated with more than one profile id is an error.

email_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing email causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have emails, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

For the 10-second limit, `Retry-After` tells you how many seconds to wait before you send the request again. A full queue doesn't set `Retry-After`. post.description:
Cancel a trigger you [scheduled](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/) with `scheduled_at`, before it fires.

The request fails if the broadcast has started calculating its audience, is already sending, or has already sent. A trigger with a `rate_limit` is the exception: you can cancel it while it sends. Canceling stops more people from entering the broadcast, and people who already entered continue through your workflow.

rate_limit.description: The rate limit you set when you triggered the broadcast. We omit this field if you didn't set one.

get.description:
Returns the operations in an automation workflow. Each object in the response represents an action or 'tile' in the automation builder.

This endpoint returns up to 10 `actions` at a time. If there is another page of results, the response will include a `next` string. Pass this string as the `start` parameter to get the next page of results.

You get the actions that have content, like messages, attribute updates, and events—not delays or flow control blocks like t/f branches.

If a message block contains multiple languages, this endpoint returns an object for each language variant. Each language variant includes the `multi_language_branch_action_id` property with the same value. Use this id to retrieve metrics for each language variant in a single request through [Get automation action metrics](/integrations/api/app/tag/automations/campaignActionMetrics/).

actions.description: Each object in the array represents an action in your automation.

bcc.description: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

body.description: The body of the action. You cannot modify the body if you created it with our drag-and-drop editor.

body_amp.description: AMP-enabled content for your email. If a recipient's email client doesn't support AMP, they receive your `body` content instead. Make sure you're [set up to send AMP](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/amp-for-email/) first.

cc.description: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

deduplicate_id.description: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was updated.

fake_bcc.description: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

from.description: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

from_id.description: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender". Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

headers.description: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`. Names and values must be strings, with no non-ASCII characters or spaces. You can't overwrite reserved headers.

id.description: The identifier for an action.

language.description: The language variant for your message. If you don't use our [localization feature](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started), or this is the default message, this value is an empty string.

layout.description: The layout used for the action, if it exists.

multi_language_branch_action_id.description: Returned when the action is a language variant of a multi-language message. This id is the same for each variant of a message, so you can use this to retrieve metrics for a message and all its variants.

name.description: The name of the action, if it exists.

parent_action_id.description: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

preheader_text.description: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

preprocessor.description: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`. Note, Juice replaced Premailer as the pre-processor, but you will only see `premailer` as the value.

recipient.description: The recipient address for an action.

reply_to.description: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

reply_to_id.description: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable. Use [List sender identities](/integrations/api/app/tag/sender-identities/listSenders/) to find valid IDs.

sending_state.description: Determines the sending behavior for the action. `automatic` sends the action automatically when triggered; `draft` queues drafts when the action is triggered; or `off` to disable the action.

subject.description: The subject line for an `email` action.
subject.example: Did you get that thing I sent you?

get.description:
Returns metrics for an individual action, both in total and as a series of counts, oldest first—the 0-index of any result is the oldest point in the window.

**We recommend version 2. Send `version=2`.** It accepts an explicit `start`, `end`, and `res`, reported in the `tz` you choose. Without it, the endpoint answers with version 1 behavior instead: a window built from `period` and `steps`, always in Eastern time.

Version 1 can't return fewer than 2 steps of any period. `?period=days&steps=1` means two days—the 48 hours before the request—and `?period=days&steps=0` returns the maximum for the period, the same as `?period=days&steps=45`.

**Multi-language messages**

If the action is a [multi-language](/messaging/channels/localization/getting-started/) message, you can retrieve metrics for a single language variant or all language variants. To retrieve metrics for a single language variant, pass the `id` of the action. To retrieve aggregate metrics and a breakdown for each language variant, pass the `multi_language_branch_action_id`, which is the same for each variant of a message. You can get both ids from the [List automation actions](/integrations/api/app/tag/automations/listCampaignActions/) endpoint.

If you pass the `multi_language_branch_action_id`, then the `metric` object shows the *total* across every variant. The `language_variants` object shows a breakdown for each language variant. 

If you want to get the sum of all metrics across all of an automation's actions, you can use each action id of a multi-language message, like you would for other types of actions.

end.description: The end of the window we reported on, in ISO 8601 format.

default.description: Whether this is the default variant. Exactly one variant per multi-language message is the default, and it always has an empty `language`.

language.description: The language code for this variant, such as `es` or `fr-CA`. Empty for the default variant—the one that people fall back to when no other variant matches their language.

series.description: Metrics grouped by the requested resolution. Each property is an array where each entry represents one period, such as one day.

machine_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails attributed to machines—security scanners, bot user agents, known proxy services, and repetitive click patterns. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

get.description:
Returns a list of Journey Metrics for your automation. These metrics show how many people triggered your automation, were messaged, etc for the time period and "resolution" you set. You must provide the `start`, `end`, and `resolution` parameters or your request will return `400`.

Metrics in the response are arrays, and each index in the array corresponds to the `resolution` in your request. If you request metrics in `days`, the first result in each metric array is the first day of results and each successive increment represents another day.

Each increment represents the number of journeys that started within a time period and eventually achieved a particular metric. For example, array index 0 for the `converted` metric represents the number of journeys that started on the first day/month of results that achieved a conversion.

activated.description: People who started a journey and were not filtered out before they experienced an action.

converted.description: People who matched the conversion criteria for the automation.

exited_early.description: People who started a journey but stopped meeting the automation trigger/filter criteria.

messaged.description: People who experienced at least one non-delay action in the journey. This metric typically represents journeys in progress.

never_activated.description: People who started a journey but were filtered out before they could experience any of the actions in the journey.

started.description: The total number of people who meet the trigger criteria for a journey. This count occurs before filters are applied.

200.description: Each `journey_metric` item in the response is an array. Each item in a metric array represents the number of journeys that started within the time increment ("resolution"—day or month) and eventually achieved that metric.

post.description:
Connect a bucket in Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage so that you can load files from it into your collections. After you connect a source, send its `id` and a file `path` to [write to a collection](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/submitCollectionWrite/), or [sync a collection](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/putCollectionSync/) to load new or changed files from a folder on a schedule.

Your credentials need permission to list and read the bucket:

- **S3:** `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:GetObject`.
- **Google Cloud Storage:** the Storage Object Viewer role.
- **Azure:** a container SAS URL that grants read and list (`sp=rl`).

Before Customer.io saves the source, it lists the bucket under your `prefix` and reads the first file it finds. If the bucket has no files under the prefix yet, Customer.io can only check that your credentials list the bucket. Customer.io encrypts your credentials and never returns them.

put.description:
Update the `name` or replace the contents of a collection. Updating the `data` or `url` for your collection fully replaces the contents of the collection.

To set or change the collection's key field or delete field without replacing its rows, send `key_field` or `delete_field` without `data` or `url`. You can send both in one request. To remove either field, send an empty string. Changing either field can mean copying every row, so Customer.io queues the change as a write request and responds with a `202` and the write's `id`. Use [get a write's status](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/getCollectionWrite/) to see when the change is done. If a row is missing a key or repeats another row's key, the write fails with the code `invalid-data`, and its `message` names the row. If you send a field that's already set, Customer.io doesn't queue anything and responds with a `200`.

When you replace the rows of a large collection, Customer.io changes only the rows that differ, and saves them in batches. While the replacement operation runs, a read can return some new rows alongside old ones. If a large replacement stops partway and can't finish, the collection is left part old and part new. Until you replace the rows again, writes fail with the code `replace-unfinished`.

**Note**:
* If you reference your collection by name in active automation messages, changing the name of the collection will cause references to the previous name to return an empty data set.
* A collection that you upload or send in an API request can be up to 10 MB. A collection that you load from files, with write requests or a sync, can be larger: each file can be up to 500 MB and 1,000,000 rows. Each top-level field in a row can hold up to 10,000 characters. The total size of all collections in your account can't exceed 5 GB. Customer.io rejects a request that would take your account over that limit.

data.description: An array of data objects that you want to reference in this collection.

delete_field.description: An attribute that marks a row for deletion, like `deleted`. When a row in a write request or a synced file sets this attribute to `true`, or to the text `true`, `1`, or `yes` in any case, Customer.io deletes the row with the same key instead of saving it. Deleting a key that doesn't exist does nothing. Customer.io never keeps a row that this attribute marks. When you create or replace a collection, Customer.io leaves marked rows out. When you set a delete field on an existing collection, Customer.io deletes the rows it already marks. A row that isn't marked keeps the attribute as you sent it. The delete field can't be the same as the key field. Send an empty string to remove it.

key_field.description: The attribute that holds each row's unique key, like `sku`, similar to a primary key in a database table. Set a key field to add, change, delete, or read individual rows without replacing the whole collection. Each row needs a unique, non-empty string or number in this attribute, up to 1,024 bytes.

put.description:
Watch a folder in one of your [collection sources](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/createCollectionSource/), and have Customer.io load each new or changed file in the folder into the collection. Customer.io saves and deletes rows by key, the same way as a [write operation](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/submitCollectionWrite/), so the collection needs a key field. A collection can have exactly one sync.

Each time Customer.io checks the folder, it loads every file that it hasn't loaded yet, plus every file that you overwrote since Customer.io loaded it, in alphabetical order of their paths, up to 2,000 files at a time. You can write a new file for each export or overwrite the same file. If you write new files, start each name with the date and time (`2026-11-03T0600-products.csv`), so that Customer.io loads them in the order that you wrote them. If you delete a file that Customer.io loaded and put it back, Customer.io loads it again. The folder can hold up to 100,000 files; past that, the sync's `state` becomes `failed` until you move files out of the folder.

Customer.io checks each file before it saves any of the file's rows. Customer.io loads the valid rows and records rejected rows, which you can look up with [list rejected sync rows](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/getCollectionSyncRejects/). If two rows in a file have the same key, Customer.io loads the first one and rejects the second. If Customer.io can't load a whole file, like when the file is too large or isn't JSON or CSV, the sync's `state` becomes `failed`, and Customer.io tries that file again at each later check. To get the sync going again, overwrite the file with one that Customer.io can load, or delete the file.

To change a sync, send it again. If you change only `poll_hours`, the sync keeps its place. If you change the source or the `prefix`, the sync starts over from the first file in the folder.

poll_hours.description: How often Customer.io checks the folder for new or changed files, in hours.

prefix.description: The folder to watch, relative to the source's own `prefix`, like `daily/`. Customer.io adds a trailing `/` if you leave it off. Leave out `prefix` to watch every file the source can read. The folder can't leave the source's prefix, so it can't contain `..` or `\`.

source_id.description: The `id` of the source to read files from.

post.description:
Add, update, or delete rows by key, without replacing the whole collection. The collection needs a [key field](/messaging/objects-data/collections/#key-fields), which you can set when you [update a collection](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/updateCollection/). A row whose key already exists replaces the old row, and a row with a new key is added. To replace every row instead, use [update a collection](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/updateCollection/).

To delete rows, give the collection a `delete_field`, like `deleted`. A row that sets that field to `true` deletes the row with the same key. A row that doesn't set it to `true` is saved with the field as you sent it. One write request can save some rows and delete others.

Send the rows in one of three ways: in the request as `data`, as a file at a `url`, or as a file in one of your [collection sources](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/listCollectionSources/) with `source_id` and `path`. Customer.io reads a file when the write runs, so a file can hold far more rows than a request body can.

Customer.io queues the write and responds right away with a write `id`, so large writes don't time out. Customer.io applies writes to a collection one at a time, in the order it receives them. Use [look up a collection write](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/getCollectionWrite/) to check the result.

Customer.io checks every row before it saves anything. If any row is invalid, Customer.io doesn't save any of them. Customer.io can handle a write of up to 500 rows all at once. If your request is larger, we apply writes 500 rows at a time. While a large write runs, a read can return some of its rows and not others. If a large write fails partway, the rows it saved stay in the collection, and you can safely send the same write again.

delete.description: For a collection whose key field is `sku` and whose delete field is `deleted`.
delete.summary: Update one row and delete another

source.summary: Write rows from a file in a source

data.description: The rows to write. Each row is an object that holds the collection's key field.

url.description: The `http` or `https` URL of your CSV or JSON file, like a signed URL to a file in your own storage. Customer.io detects the format from the `Content-Type` that your URL returns, or from the file extension if the `Content-Type` doesn't say. JSON data can be an array of objects or one object per line. CSV data needs a header row, and Customer.io reads every CSV value as a string. A file can be up to 500 MB and 1,000,000 rows.

path.description: The file's path, relative to the source's `prefix`, like `daily/products.csv`. Use forward slashes. The path can't leave the prefix, so it can't contain `..` or `\`. Customer.io reads the file the same way it reads a file from a `url`.

source_id.description: The `id` of the [collection source](/integrations/api/app/tag/collections/createCollectionSource/) that holds the file.

code.description: If the write request's `state` is `failed`, the code explains why. A write of up to 500 rows saves nothing when it fails, and a larger write keeps the rows it saved before it failed. `source-refused` means Customer.io couldn't download the file, or the source is gone or unusable. `replace-unfinished` means an earlier replacement stopped partway, so you need to replace the collection's rows again.

id.description: The identifier for the write request. Use it to look up the write's status.

items.description: For a write request that failed with `items`, up to 500 of the rows that Customer.io rejected. Customer.io didn't save any of the rows.

code.description: Why the row failed.

index.description: The row's position in the write request, starting at 0. For a write that sends `data`, this is the row's position in the `data` array. For a write from a file, this is the row's position among the file's rows.

key.description: The row's key, if it has one.

message.description: A readable explanation of the failure.

state.description: Where the write request stands. `replaced` means that a later replacement of the whole collection ran first, so the collection ends up as if this write ran before the replacement.

404.description: The collection `id` does not exist.

422.description: Customer.io couldn't accept the write request, and didn't queue it. The response explains what to fix. When a row in `data` is invalid, each error's `source.pointer` names the row, like `/data/attributes/data/1`. Customer.io checks the rows in a file when the write runs, so a problem in a file shows up in the write's result instead.

post.description:
Provide a filter to search for people in your workspace. Your filter can filter people by segment (using the Segment ID) and attribute values; when you filter by attributes, you can use `eq` (matching an attribute value) or `exists` (matching when a person has the attribute). Use the `and` array, `or` array, and `not` object to create a complex filter. The `not` selector is an object that takes a single filter.

Returns arrays of `identifiers` and `ids`. In general, you should rely on the newer `identifiers` array, which contains more complete information about each person captured by the filter in your request, than the `ids` array, which only contains `id` values.

You can return up to 1000 people per request. If you want to return a larger set of people in a single request, you may want to use the [`/exports`](/integrations/api/app/tag/exports/) API instead.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* meet the condition.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

not.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

servers.description: This API uses bearer authorization, requiring a [token that you generate in the UI](https://fly.customer.io/settings/api_credentials?keyType=app).

post.description: Return attributes and devices for up to 100 customers by ID. If an ID in the request does not exist, the response omits it.

parameters.description: The type of `customer_id` you want to use to reference a person. If you don't provide this parameter, we assume that the `customer_id` in your request is a person's `id`. You can use `email` and `phone` only if they're enabled as identifiers in your [workspace settings](/accounts/workspaces/overview/#migrate-workspace); otherwise the request returns `400`. Reference `phone` values in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164), like `+14155552671`, and URL-encode the leading `+` as `%2B`.
parameters.name: id_type

ids.description: An array of up to 100 customer identifiers. All values must match the `id_type` query parameter—`id` values by default.

customer.description: The profile you referenced by ID in the request.

additionalProperties.description: Non-identifier attributes assigned to this person.

attributes.description: Contains attributes assigned to this profile, including your workspace's people-identifiers (by default, these are `id`, `email`, and `cio_id`). Attributes are all stored as strings.

_cio_subscription_preferences_computed.description: A person's computed subscription preferences as stringified JSON, combining set preferences with defaults for unset topics. [Learn more about backfilled preferences](/messaging/channels/subscriptions/center/#backfill-preferences).

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

cio_subscription_preferences.description: A person's subscription preferences as stringified JSON. If unset, preferences are computed from topic defaults; see `_cio_subscription_preferences_computed`.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

devices.description: Lists the devices associated with the customer profile.

items.description: Device properties collected by [Customer.io SDKs](/integrations/sdk/) unless `autoTrackDeviceAttributes` is disabled. You can use these properties in segments and Liquid.

additionalProperties.description: Custom properties that you want to associate with the device.

attributes.description: Attributes that you can reference to segment your audience—like a person's attributes, but specific to a device. These can be either the attributes defined below or custom key-value attributes.

_last_status.description: The delivery status of the last message sent to the device—sent, bounced, or suppressed. An empty string indicates that that the device hasn't received a push yet.

app_identifier.description: The app that the device belongs to—the **Bundle ID / App identifier** you entered with that app's push credentials. If you have more than one app, we use this attribute to send push notifications to the right app. A device without an app identifier receives push notifications you send to your [default app](/messaging/channels/push/getting-started/#the-default-app).

app_version.description: The version of your app that a customer uses. You might target app versions to let people know when they need to update, or expose them to new features when they do.

cio_sdk_version.description: The version of the Customer.io SDK in the app.

device_locale.description: The device's [IETF language code](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started/#supported-languages), such as `en-MX` or `es-ES`.

device_model.description: The model of the device a person uses.

device_os.description: The operating system, including the version, on the device.

push_enabled.description: If `"true"`, the device is opted-in and can receive push notifications.

id.description: The unique device identifier. This is an APNs token, an FCM registration token, or a [Firebase Installation ID (FID)](/messaging/channels/push/developer-guide/#device-ids).

last_used.description: The `timestamp` when you last identified this device. If you don't pass a timestamp when you add or update a device, we use the time of the request itself. Our SDKs identify a device when a person launches their app.

token_type.description: Used with FCM. This represents the kind of ID in the device's `id` field, either `fid` for a [Firebase Installation ID](/messaging/channels/push/developer-guide/#device-ids) or `token` for an FCM registration token. This field is not used with APNs. See [Token types](/messaging/channels/push/developer-guide/#token-types) to learn how Customer.io supports each kind of ID.

id.description: The customer ID referenced in the request.

identifiers.description: Identifiers for the person in a response—`id`, `cio_id`, and `email`. Unset `id` or `email` values are `null`. We recommend this object over the less descriptive `customer_id`. This object doesn't include `phone`, even if your workspace uses phone numbers as an identifier; look for the person's `phone` attribute instead.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

email.description: A person's email address, if set.

id.description: A person's unique ID, if set. This is the same as the `customer_id` if present.

timestamps.description: The epoch timestamps when corresponding attributes were set on the customer profile.

_cio_subscription_preferences_computed.description: Because this value is computed and not actually set on a person, this value is always 0

_last_emailed.description: The date-time when you last emailed a person.

additionalProperties.description: Timestamps when attributes assigned to the person were set.

cio_id.description: The date-time when `cio_id` was assigned.

cio_subscription_preferences.description: The datetime when a person's subscription preferences were last updated.

email.description: The date-time when the person's email address was added.

id.description: The date-time when the person's ID was generated.

unsubscribed.description: The date-time when the person unsubscribed.
If `true`, a person is globally unsubscribed from email, SMS, WhatsApp, and push. Values like `true`, `TRUE`, `1`, and `"1"` count as true; other values are treated as subscribed or topic-based.

get.description:
Return a list of activities performed by, or for, a customer. Activities are things like attribute changes and message sends.

This endpoint is guaranteed to return activity history within the past 30 days. It might return data older than 30 days in some circumstances, but activites older than 30 days are not guaranteed.

customer_id.description: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI. If your workspace supports multiple identifiers (email and ID), this value can be null.

customer_identifiers.description: Identifiers for the person in a response—`id`, `cio_id`, and `email`. Unset `id` or `email` values are `null`. We recommend this object over the less descriptive `customer_id`. This object doesn't include `phone`, even if your workspace uses phone numbers as an identifier; look for the person's `phone` attribute instead.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

email.description: A person's email address, if set.

id.description: A person's unique ID, if set. This is the same as the `customer_id` if present.

delivered.description: The date-time when the message was delivered, if applicable.

delivery_id.description: The message ID.

opened.description: Indicates whether or not a customer opened a message, if the message was delivered.

from.description: The old attribute value. If empty, the customer probably didn't bear the attribute before this action.

oneOf.description: The name of the object is the attribute that changed.
oneOf.title: Attribute change

oneOf.description: The data for a `consent` activity. The activity's `name` is the action, `opted_in` or `opted_out`. Customer.io fills in the optional fields when the change that created the record has that information. See [Consent records](/messaging/channels/subscriptions/consent-records/#what-a-record-contains).

channel.description: The channel the consent applies to, like `email` or `sms`. Absent when the consent applies to all of your messages.

collection_point.description: Where the change came from, like your subscription center or an SMS reply. The `subscription_preference_migration` and `sender_optout_migration` values mark records that Customer.io imported from preferences and opt-outs that existed before your account recorded consent.

consent_state.description: The state the change left the person in.

delivery_id.description: The message the person responded to, like the email that contained the unsubscribe link.

from.description: The sender's email address or phone number when the change happened.

profile_identifier.description: The identifier your request used to find the person.

received_on.description: The address or phone number the person's reply came from.

response.description: What the person sent back, like the body of an SMS reply.

sender_id.description: The sender identity the consent applies to, if any.

source_event_id.description: The ID of the activity that produced this record, like the inbound SMS that contained STOP.

topic_id.description: The subscription topic the consent applies to, if any.

topic_name.description: The topic's name when the change happened. Renaming the topic later doesn't change this value.

oneOf.title: Consent record

delivery_id.description: The message ID.

id.description: The identifier for the action.

name.description: The name of the event, for `event` and `screen` activities. For `consent` activities, the consent action, which is `opted_in`, `opted_out`, or `voided`.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the action occurred.

type.description: The type of activity. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

url.description: The page URL, for `page` activities.

200.description: Returns an array of activity objects. Each object represents an activity that the customer performed, or that you performed on behalf of the customer.

Returns information about the deliveries sent to a person. Provide query parameters to refine the data you want to return.

Use the `start_ts` and `end_ts` to find messages within a time range. If your request doesn't include `start_ts` and `end_ts` parameters, we'll return the most recent 6 months of messages. post.description:
Attributes are customer data like their name and email. Use this endpoint to add new attributes or update existing attributes in your workspace. To add attributes to customers, use our Pipelines or Track APIs. **NOTE:** If you add new attributes, they will not appear in your [Data Index](/journeys/people/find/using-data-index/) until you've added it to a customer's profile.

Add descriptions for attributes [so our AI tools can better understand your data](/ai/cio-with-llms/). For instance, this influences how our segment builder generates conditions with AI.

If you're on a Premium plan, you can also specify [whether an attribute is sensitive or not](/accounts/settings/team/intro-account-access/#hide-sensitive-attributes). Then Admins and Workspace Admins can decide which teammates to hide sensitive data from.

get.description:
Find addresses that the email service provider (ESP) suppressed because of bounces or spam reports.

You can get up to 1000 addresses per request. Use the `offset` parameter to get addresses beyond the first 1000.

Only `bounces` and `spam_reports` return addresses. `suppressions` is `null` for `blocks`, `invalid_emails`, or when no addresses match. When `suppressions` is `null`, the response has no `category`.

If you have multiple sending domains, we recommend querying for each domain separately, as an email address may be suppressed on multiple domains.

**Note**: If you have a large number of suppressions, consider using the [Get ESP-suppressed emails by domain](/integrations/api/app/tag/esp-suppression/getDomainSuppressionsByType/) endpoint. It's more performant for large datasets.

post.description:
Provide filters for the one-time send, automation, or action you want to return delivery information from. This endpoint starts an export, but you cannot download your export from this endpoint. Use the `/exports/{export_id}` endpoint to download your export.

Use the `start` and `end` to find messages within a time range. If your request doesn't include `start` and `end` parameters, we'll return the most recent 6 months of messages. If you filter by a one-time send, we return every delivery from that send instead. If your `start` and `end` range is more than 1 year, we reject the request with a `400` error. Timestamps reflect when deliveries were created in our system, not when they were actually sent to recipients. There may be a delay between creation and sending.

post.description:
This endpoint lets you upload a file containing people, events, objects, relationships, or geofences. It provides a handy way of adding and updating them in bulk. Uploading people, objects, or relationships is like performing an [`identify` call](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/entity/) for each row in your CSV; uploading events is like performing a [`track` call](/integrations/api/track/tag/track-events/track/). Uploading geofences adds or updates them in a geofence set, the same way an import in the UI does. Geofence imports are available on Premium and Enterprise plans.

You'll need to provide us the public URL of your file as a part of this operation. We recommend that you host your files from short-lived URLs. Ideally, your URLs will expire 2 hours after you initiate an import so that your customers' information doesn't remain publicly available after you've uploaded it to us.

Check out the file requirements based on what you're importing: [people](/journeys/people/uploading-people/#csv-requirements), [events](/journeys/people/uploading-people/#event-csv-requirements), [objects or relationships](/journeys/objects-data/objects/import-objects/#csv-requirements), and [geofences](/messaging/people/location/import-geofences/).

This endpoint performs some basic validation on the request and then queues the import for processing. The import happens in multiple stages after your request, and may even fail. You'll need to [lookup the status of the import](/integrations/api/app/tag/imports/getImport/) to check on its progress.

Records in your file might result in errors or warnings during the import. We make the errors and warnings available in CSV files that you can download via our export endpoints. [Lookup your import](/integrations/api/app/tag/imports/getImport/) to get download URLs for error and warning reports.

post.description:
End a running activity, referenced by its `instance_id`. On iOS, the system dismisses the activity from the Lock Screen. On Android, the SDK normally renders the final content as a non-ongoing notification; it cancels the notification only when there's no final notification to render. You can include a final `content_state` to show before the activity ends.

`push_payload` is optional on the end call, whether Customer.io delivers directly through APNs or relays through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). If you include a `push_payload.alert`, it must contain both a `title` and a `body`.

post.description:
Start a live notification for a profile. Customer.io mints an `instance_id` for the new activity and returns it. You'll use this ID to update, end, or check the status of the activity.

[On iOS](/integrations/sdk/ios/live-activities/set-up/#step-5-start-an-activity), this delivers a push-to-start event through APNs, so the person's device must have a registered push-to-start token for the `notification_type` (the SDK registers one automatically when your app registers the activity type). Push-to-start requires iOS 17.2 or later. iOS starts also require a `push_payload.alert` with a title and body.

[On Android](/integrations/sdk/android/live-notifications/set-up/#step-4-start-a-notification), this delivers an FCM data message, which the SDK renders without your app being open.

This only matters when your workspace has multiple apps: set it to target a device belonging to that app, or omit it to target the workspace's default app. Workspaces without multiple apps ignore this field. If you provide a value that doesn't match an app in your workspace, the request fails with a `400`.

get.description:
Return a list of deliveries, including metrics for each delivery, for messages in your workspace. The request body contains filters determining the deliveries you want to return information about.

Use the `start_ts` and `end_ts` parameters to find messages within a time range. We limit your requests to 6 months. If your request doesn't include `start_ts` and `end_ts` parameters, we'll return the most recent 6 months of deliveries. If `start_ts` is greater than 6-months before `end_ts`, we only send back 6 months of data. If only `end_ts` is specified, we return 6 months of data before this timestamp. If only `start_ts` is specified, we set `end_ts` to the current time and return data from `start_ts` onward, limited to the most recent 6 months. Timestamps reflect when deliveries were created in our system, not when they were actually sent to recipients. There may be a delay between creation and sending.

recipient_segment_ids.description: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.
- If you send immediately instead of scheduling, there's a short delay before Customer.io starts sending. During that delay, `scheduled_at` isn't `null` and isn't a future time: it's the time you made the request, an earlier time, or `0`.
- While Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until its segments finish building, this is the next time Customer.io checks the segments.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started. A scheduled send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `scheduled`.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered. A send-now send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `sending`.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.

post.description:
Create a one-time send (referred to as a "newsletter" in our APIs) and optionally schedule it or send it immediately.

Set the audience with either `recipients` (a filter over segments and profile attributes) or `recipient_file_url` (a CSV of recipients). One of the two is required, and a request carrying both is rejected.

To send it immediately, set `send_now` to `true`. To schedule for later, set `scheduled_at` to a Unix timestamp in the future. If you don't set either, it's created as a draft.

If you set `send_now` or `scheduled_at` and a recipient segment is still building, Customer.io accepts the request and [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until the segment finishes. The [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) and [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) endpoints describe what the one-time send reports while Customer.io holds it.

A `recipient_file_url` audience resolves in the background, so you can't send or schedule in the same request. Poll [Get a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/getNewsletters/) until `recipient_file_status` is `done`, then call [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/).

There's no endpoint that updates a one-time send, so `name`, the audience, and `deduped` are fixed once you create it. To change them on a draft, delete it and create a new one. You can still edit content through the [variant endpoints](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletter-variants/listNewsletterVariants/) until it sends.

If you [enabled a subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/#enable-sub-center) in your workspace, `subscription_topic_id` is required. Use the [subscription center endpoint](/integrations/api/app/tag/subscription-center/getTopics/) to find IDs.

Use standard HTML/CSS for the `body` of an email; this endpoint can't pull in global style variables or render our Design Studio's component syntax. You can create Design Studio emails through [other endpoints](/integrations/api/design-studio/). All requests must be less than 1 MB.

Product Updates

Here's what we shipped this week...

value.preheader_text: Check out our latest features and improvements
value.subject: What's new this week, {{ customer.first_name }}

body.description: The HTML body content of the email. Use standard HTML/CSS, not syntax unique to Design Studio.

body_plain.description: The plaintext body of the email. If provided, this overwrites the auto-generated plaintext.

deduped.description: When `true`, Customer.io sends only one message per email address or phone number, even when several profiles share it. Supported on `email`, `twilio`, and `sms` one-time sends. If the send's address is an identifier in your workspace (email for `email` sends, phone number for `twilio` and `sms` sends), Customer.io returns a 422 when you set `deduped` to `true`, because no two profiles can share an identifier and there's nothing to dedupe. layout_id.description: The ID of the [layout](/journeys/channels/email/layouts/3-layouts-and-customerio/) you want to use for the email. If you don't set one, the email uses your workspace's default layout. Find a layout's ID in its URL.

recipients.description:
Filter conditions that define the one-time send's recipients. In `recipients`, you can combine `segment` and `attribute` conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not` operators.

This endpoint enforces a strict shape:

* The outermost object must be a single `and` array.
* Every operator or condition object takes exactly **one** key: `and`, `or`, `not`, `segment`, or `attribute`. An object with two keys—like `not` alongside `and`—is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.
* Segment conditions must be wrapped in an `or` array, even for a single segment—and `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.
* To exclude segments, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array.
* Attribute conditions sit directly in the `and` array, unwrapped. To negate an attribute condition, set `inverse: true` on the attribute itself—`not` can't contain attribute conditions.

The email example on this operation shows or-wrapped segments combined with a negated attribute; for the common "include segment A, exclude segment B" pattern, see the **include one segment, exclude another** request example. See [Format API-triggered broadcasts](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-data-format/#overriding-recipients) for general operator behavior.

inverse.description: Set to `true` for "is not equal" or "does not exist".

operator.description: The comparison operator.

value.description: The value to compare against. Required when `operator` is `eq`.

not.description: A condition or group of conditions to exclude. On this endpoint, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array. An object with both `and` and `not` keys is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.

body_json.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.
- If you send immediately instead of scheduling, there's a short delay before Customer.io starts sending. During that delay, `scheduled_at` isn't `null` and isn't a future time: it's the time you made the request, an earlier time, or `0`.
- While Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until its segments finish building, this is the next time Customer.io checks the segments.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started. A scheduled send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `scheduled`.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered. A send-now send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `sending`.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.

422.description:

- Missing or invalid `subscription_topic_id` (required when a subscription center is enabled)
- Invalid `from_id` or unverified/malformed `from` address
- Both `from_id` and `from` provided (use one or the other)
- Invalid channel `type`
- Missing required content fields for the channel type (`subject`, `body`, `body_json`, `request_method`, `url`)

- Sender uses a transactional IP pool
- Recipients include a temporary segment

get.description:
Returns a metrics for an individual one-time send (referred to as a "newsletter" in our APIs) variant—either an individual language in a multi-language one-time send or a message in an A/B test. This endpoint returns metrics both in total and in `steps` (days, weeks, etc) over a `period` of time. Stepped `series` metrics are arranged from oldest to newest (i.e. the 0-index for any result is the oldest period/step).

You cannot request fewer than 2 steps of any period (2 hours, 2 days, 2 weeks, or 2 months). For instance, `?period=days&steps=1` means two days - the 48 hours before the API request was made. `?period=days&steps=0` returns the same as the maximum of the period - `?period=days&steps=45`. See the `steps` parameter below for the maximum count of each period.

series.description: Metrics grouped by the requested resolution. Each property is an array where each entry represents one period, such as one day.

clicked.description: The number of `clicked` messages.

created.description: The number of `created` messages.

delivered.description: The number of `delivered` messages.

human_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails excluding machine clicks. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

human_opened.description: The number of `opened` emails excluding machine opens. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

link_untracked.description: The number of emails delivered with link tracking inactive for any reason. We subtract these from the click-rate denominator.

machine_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails attributed to machines—security scanners, bot user agents, known proxy services, and repetitive click patterns. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

open_untracked.description: The number of emails delivered with open tracking inactive for any reason—including the consent opt-outs that `untracked` counts and messages sent with open tracking disabled. We subtract these from the open-rate denominator.

opened.description: The number of `opened` messages.

prefetch_opened.description: The number of `opened` emails attributed to machines. This metric is reliable starting March 20, 2025.

replied.description: The number of SMS/MMS messages a person replied to with a keyword. [Learn more about inbound messages](/messaging/channels/sms/inbound/get-started/).

spammed.description: The number of spam complaints.

topic_unsubscribed.description: The number of topic unsubscribes in a given period.

tracking_consent_denied.description: The number of people who denied consent to email open tracking in the period.

tracking_consent_granted.description: The number of people who granted consent to email open tracking in the period.

unsubscribed.description: The number of unsubscribes attributed to the automation or message.

untracked.description: The number of `sent` emails whose open pixel we withheld because the person opted out of open tracking. We exclude these from the open-rate denominator; click tracking is unaffected.

recipient_segment_ids.description: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.
- If you send immediately instead of scheduling, there's a short delay before Customer.io starts sending. During that delay, `scheduled_at` isn't `null` and isn't a future time: it's the time you made the request, an earlier time, or `0`.
- While Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until its segments finish building, this is the next time Customer.io checks the segments.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started. A scheduled send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `scheduled`.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered. A send-now send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `sending`.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.

get.description:
Returns information about the "deliveries" (rendered messages) sent to your recipients for a specific one-time send (referred to as a "newsletter" in our APIs).

Provide query parameters to refine the metrics you want to return. Use `start_ts` and `end_ts` to find messages within a time range. If your request doesn't include either `start_ts` or `end_ts`, we'll return every message from the one-time send, from when it started sending through its last delivery. If your `start_ts` and `end_ts` range is more than 6 months, we'll return 6 months of data from the most recent timestamp in your request.

Timestamps reflect when deliveries were created in our system, not when they were actually sent to recipients. There may be a delay between creation and sending.

post.description:
Schedule a one-time send (referred to as a "newsletter" in our APIs) to send at a specific time. It must be in a draft state. If it has already been sent, you'll get a `400` error. If it's already scheduled, this endpoint updates the scheduled time.

The response returns the one-time send, so you can read back the schedule you set: `send_state` and `scheduled_at` are always included, and `timezone` and `tz_match_enabled` are included when they apply.

To retrieve the schedule parameters after scheduling with [Get a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/getNewsletters/). After you start a send with timezone-match, `scheduled_at` reports the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test instead of the time you requested.

If a recipient segment is still building at the scheduled time, Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until the segment finishes. While Customer.io holds it, `send_state` stays `scheduled` and `scheduled_at` is the next time Customer.io checks the segments. If the segments don't finish building within 6 hours, the one-time send returns to `drafted` without sending any messages. A schedule with `tz_match_enabled` set to `true` doesn't wait, so you can't make that request while a recipient segment is still building.

The recipients are fixed when you create the one-time send. If you're not sure who will receive it, you can use the [List one-time sends](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/listNewsletters/) endpoint to get a list of one-time sends and their recipients.

schema.description: Only `scheduled_at` is required. If you want to send with a rate limit, set both `rate_limit_email_rate` or `rate_limit_time_period`. `rate_limit_spread` can be set alone.

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds measured from the scheduled time, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes. You can't combine it with `tz_match_enabled`, with send time optimization, or with descheduling (`scheduled_at` of `0`), and on an A/B test it must outlast the test duration.

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp for the send. Use `0` to deschedule. When greater than `0`, the time must be in the future and you must send `timezone` so the UI displays the time correctly.

timezone.description: [IANA timezone name](/journeys/send/timezones/example-timezones/#region-format) (for example, `America/New_York`). Required when `scheduled_at` is greater than `0`. Not required when descheduling (`scheduled_at` is `0`).

tz_match_enabled.description: When `true`, sends at the same local time in each recipient's timezone. If it's set to `true` and `rate_limit_time_period` is provided, then the period can't be greater than `3600` (1 hour).

content_ids.description: A list of message variants in a one-time send, where a variant is a translation or A/B test.

created.description: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

deduplicate_id.description: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was updated.

expires_after.description: The send window in seconds, if you set one. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send this long after it starts.

id.description: The identifier for a one-time send.

name.description: The name of the one-time send. Must be 190 characters or less.

recipient_file_error.description: Why the recipient file failed, when `recipient_file_status` is `error`. Customer.io omits it otherwise.

recipient_file_status.description: How far Customer.io has got with a recipient file, whether you uploaded it in the UI or passed `recipient_file_url`. Customer.io omits this field when the audience came from a `recipients` filter. Wait for `done` before you send or schedule.

recipient_segment_ids.description: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.
- If you send immediately instead of scheduling, there's a short delay before Customer.io starts sending. During that delay, `scheduled_at` isn't `null` and isn't a future time: it's the time you made the request, an earlier time, or `0`.
- While Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until its segments finish building, this is the next time Customer.io checks the segments.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started. A scheduled send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `scheduled`.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered. A send-now send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `sending`.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.

sent_at.description: The last time the one-time send was sent, or `null` if it hasn't been sent.

subscription_topic_id.description: If you enabled a [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/) on your workspace, this returns the id of the subscription preference you set.

tags.description: An array of tags associated with the one-time send.

timezone.description: The [IANA timezone name](/journeys/send/timezones/example-timezones/#region-format) of the schedule (for example, `America/New_York`). Customer.io includes this field only when the active schedule has a timezone. It's omitted otherwise.

type.description: Channel type for a one-time send or one-time send content variant.

tz_match_enabled.description: `true` when the pending schedule sends at the same local time in each person's timezone. Customer.io includes this field only while a timezone-match schedule is pending. It's omitted otherwise and is never `false`.

updated.description: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

Add a language variant to a specific A/B test group in a one-time send (referred to as a "newsletter" in our APIs). The new variant is a copy of the default template in the test group with the content you provide. The payload the endpoint accepts depends on the parent one-time send's channel type: if it's an email, the payload will be an email variant; if it's an SMS, the payload will be an SMS variant.

recipient_file_status.description: How far Customer.io has got with a recipient file, whether you uploaded it in the UI or passed `recipient_file_url`. Customer.io omits this field when the audience came from a `recipients` filter. Wait for `done` before you send or schedule.

recipient_segment_ids.description: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.
- If you send immediately instead of scheduling, there's a short delay before Customer.io starts sending. During that delay, `scheduled_at` isn't `null` and isn't a future time: it's the time you made the request, an earlier time, or `0`.
- While Customer.io [holds the send](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#queued-sends) until its segments finish building, this is the next time Customer.io checks the segments.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started. A scheduled send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `scheduled`.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered. A send-now send that Customer.io is holding until its segments finish building also reports `sending`.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.
